segs.e: Linked Discourses 12.1
1. The Buddhas
Dependent Origination
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, I will teach you dependent origination.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what is dependent origination?
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
This is called dependent origination.
When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases.
When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.
When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases.
When contact ceases, feeling ceases.
When feeling ceases, craving ceases.
When craving ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.
Linked Discourses 12.2
1. The Buddhas
Analysis
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach and analyze for you dependent origination.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what is dependent origination?
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
And what is old age and death?

segs.p: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṁ pāliccaṁ valittacatā āyuno saṁhāni indriyānaṁ paripāko;
segs.e: The old age, decrepitude, broken teeth, grey hair, wrinkly skin, diminished vitality, and failing faculties of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.
This is called old age.

segs.p: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṁ maccu maraṇaṁ kālakiriyā khandhānaṁ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo (…),
segs.e: The passing away, passing on, disintegration, demise, mortality, death, decease, breaking up of the aggregates, and laying to rest of the corpse of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.
This is called death.
Such is old age, and such is death.
This is called old age and death.
And what is rebirth?

segs.p: Yā tesaṁ tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti abhinibbatti khandhānaṁ pātubhāvo āyatanānaṁ paṭilābho.
segs.e: The rebirth, inception, conception, regeneration, manifestation of the aggregates, and acquisition of the sense fields of the various sentient beings in the various orders of sentient beings.
This is called rebirth.
And what is continued existence?
There are these three states of existence.
Existence in the sensual realm, the realm of luminous form, and the formless realm.
This is called continued existence.
And what is grasping?
There are these four kinds of grasping.
Grasping at sensual pleasures, views, precepts and observances, and theories of a self.
This is called grasping.
And what is craving?
There are these six classes of craving.

segs.p: rūpataṇhā, saddataṇhā, gandhataṇhā, rasataṇhā, phoṭṭhabbataṇhā, dhammataṇhā.
segs.e: Craving for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.
This is called craving.
And what is feeling?
There are these six classes of feeling.

segs.p: cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā.
segs.e: Feeling born of contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
This is called feeling.
And what is contact?
There are these six classes of contact.

segs.p: cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphasso, ghānasamphasso, jivhāsamphasso, kāyasamphasso, manosamphasso.
segs.e: Contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
This is called contact.
And what are the six sense fields?

segs.p: Cakkhāyatanaṁ, sotāyatanaṁ, ghānāyatanaṁ, jivhāyatanaṁ, kāyāyatanaṁ, manāyatanaṁ—
segs.e: The sense fields of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.
These are called the six sense fields.
And what are name and form?
Feeling, perception, intention, contact, and application of mind.
This is called name.

segs.p: Cattāro ca mahābhūtā, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṁ upādāyarūpaṁ.
segs.e: The four principal states, and form derived from the four principal states.
This is called form.
Such is name and such is form.
These are called name and form.
And what is consciousness?
There are these six classes of consciousness.

segs.p: cakkhuviññāṇaṁ, sotaviññāṇaṁ, ghānaviññāṇaṁ, jivhāviññāṇaṁ, kāyaviññāṇaṁ, manoviññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: Eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.
This is called consciousness.
And what are choices?
There are three kinds of choices.
Choices by way of body, speech, and mind.
These are called choices.
And what is ignorance?

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe aññāṇaṁ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṁ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṁ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: Not knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.
This is called ignorance.
And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
Linked Discourses 12.3
1. The Buddhas
Practice
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what’s the wrong practice?
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
This is called the wrong practice.
And what’s the right practice?
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
This is called the right practice.”
Linked Discourses 12.4
1. The Buddhas
About Vipassī
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “vipassissa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, Vipassī the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha had this thought before his awakening, when he was still unawakened but intent on awakening:

segs.p: ‘kicchaṁ vatāyaṁ loko āpanno jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca.
segs.e: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble. It’s born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn,

segs.p: Atha ca panimassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṁ nappajānāti jarāmaraṇassa.
segs.e: yet it doesn’t understand how to escape from this suffering, from old age and death.

segs.p: Kudāssu nāma imassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyissati jarāmaraṇassā’ti?
segs.e: Oh, when will an escape be found from this suffering, from old age and death?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī, the one intent on awakening, thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā jarāmaraṇan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there old age and death? What is a requirement for old age and death?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When rebirth exists there’s old age and death. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati jāti hoti, kiṁpaccayā jātī’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there rebirth? What is a requirement for rebirth?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘bhave kho sati jāti hoti, bhavapaccayā jātī’ti.
segs.e: ‘When continued existence exists there’s rebirth. Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati bhavo hoti, kiṁpaccayā bhavo’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there continued existence? What is a requirement for continued existence?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘upādāne kho sati bhavo hoti, upādānapaccayā bhavo’ti.
segs.e: ‘When grasping exists there’s continued existence. Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati upādānaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā upādānan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there grasping? What is a requirement for grasping?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘taṇhāya kho sati upādānaṁ hoti, taṇhāpaccayā upādānan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When craving exists there’s grasping. Craving is a requirement for grasping.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati taṇhā hoti, kiṁpaccayā taṇhā’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there craving? What is a requirement for craving?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘vedanāya kho sati taṇhā hoti, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘When feeling exists there’s craving. Feeling is a requirement for craving.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati vedanā hoti, kiṁpaccayā vedanā’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there feeling? What is a requirement for feeling?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘phasse kho sati vedanā hoti, phassapaccayā vedanā’ti.
segs.e: ‘When contact exists there’s feeling. Contact is a requirement for feeling.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati phasso hoti, kiṁpaccayā phasso’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there contact? What is a requirement for contact?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘saḷāyatane kho sati phasso hoti, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso’ti.
segs.e: ‘When the six sense fields exist there’s contact. The six sense fields are requirements for contact.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati saḷāyatanaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā saḷāyatanan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists are there the six sense fields? What is a requirement for the six sense fields?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘nāmarūpe kho sati saḷāyatanaṁ hoti, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When name and form exist there are the six sense fields. Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati nāmarūpaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā nāmarūpan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists are there name and form? What is a requirement for name and form?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘viññāṇe kho sati nāmarūpaṁ hoti, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When consciousness exists there are name and form. Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati viññāṇaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā viññāṇan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there consciousness? What is a requirement for consciousness?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘saṅkhāresu kho sati viññāṇaṁ hoti, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When choices exist there’s consciousness. Choices are a requirement for consciousness.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati saṅkhārā honti, kiṁpaccayā saṅkhārā’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists are there choices? What is a requirement for choices?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘avijjāya kho sati saṅkhārā honti, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā’ti.
segs.e: ‘When ignorance exists there are choices. Ignorance is a requirement for choices.’
And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: ‘Samudayo, samudayo’ti kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṁ udapādi, ñāṇaṁ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.
segs.e: ‘Origination, origination.’ While Vipassī was intent on awakening, such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in him regarding teachings not learned before from another.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no old age and death? When what ceases do old age and death cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘jātiyā kho asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hoti, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When rebirth doesn’t exist there’s no old age and death. When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati jāti na hoti, kissa nirodhā jātinirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no rebirth? When what ceases does rebirth cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘bhave kho asati jāti na hoti, bhavanirodhā jātinirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When continued existence doesn’t exist there’s no rebirth. When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati bhavo na hoti, kissa nirodhā bhavanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no continued existence? When what ceases does continued existence cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘upādāne kho asati bhavo na hoti, upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When grasping doesn’t exist there’s no continued existence. When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati upādānaṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā upādānanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no grasping? When what ceases does grasping cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘taṇhāya kho asati upādānaṁ na hoti, taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When craving doesn’t exist there’s no grasping. When craving ceases, grasping ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati taṇhā na hoti, kissa nirodhā taṇhānirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no craving? When what ceases does craving cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘vedanāya kho asati taṇhā na hoti, vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When feeling doesn’t exist there’s no craving. When feeling ceases, craving ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati vedanā na hoti, kissa nirodhā vedanānirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no feeling? When what ceases does feeling cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘phasse kho asati vedanā na hoti, phassanirodhā vedanānirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When contact doesn’t exist there’s no feeling. When contact ceases, feeling ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati phasso na hoti, kissa nirodhā phassanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no contact? When what ceases does contact cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘saḷāyatane kho asati phasso na hoti, saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When the six sense fields don’t exist there’s no contact. When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati saḷāyatanaṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā saḷāyatananirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no six sense fields? When what ceases do the six sense fields cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘nāmarūpe kho asati saḷāyatanaṁ na hoti, nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When name and form don’t exist there are no six sense fields. When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati nāmarūpaṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā nāmarūpanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no name and form? When what ceases do name and form cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘viññāṇe kho asati nāmarūpaṁ na hoti, viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When consciousness doesn’t exist there are no name and form. When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati viññāṇaṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā viññāṇanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no consciousness? When what ceases does consciousness cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘saṅkhāresu kho asati viññāṇaṁ na hoti, saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When choices don’t exist there’s no consciousness. When choices cease, consciousness ceases.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Vipassī thought:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati saṅkhārā na honti, kissa nirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no choices? When what ceases do choices cease?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, Vipassī penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘avijjāya kho asati saṅkhārā na honti, avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When ignorance doesn’t exist there are no choices. When ignorance ceases, choices cease.’
And so, when ignorance ceases, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

segs.p: ‘Nirodho, nirodho’ti kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṁ udapādi, ñāṇaṁ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādī”ti.
segs.e: ‘Cessation, cessation.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in Vipassī, the one intent on awakening, regarding teachings not learned before from another.”

Gotama

segs.p: “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

segs.p: ‘kicchaṁ vatāyaṁ loko āpanno jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca.
segs.e: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble. It’s born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn,

segs.p: Atha ca panimassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṁ nappajānāti jarāmaraṇassa.
segs.e: yet it doesn’t understand how to escape from this suffering, from old age and death.

segs.p: Kudāssu nāma imassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyissati jarāmaraṇassā’ti?
segs.e: Oh, when will an escape be found from this suffering, from old age and death?’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā jarāmaraṇan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there old age and death? What is a requirement for old age and death?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When rebirth exists there’s old age and death. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’
Then it occurred to me:
‘When what exists is there rebirth? …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
consciousness …
‘When what exists are there choices? What is a requirement for choices?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘avijjāya kho sati saṅkhārā honti, avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā’ti.
segs.e: ‘When ignorance exists there are choices. Ignorance is a requirement for choices.’
And so, ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: ‘Samudayo, samudayo’ti kho me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṁ udapādi, ñāṇaṁ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.
segs.e: ‘Origination, origination.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in me regarding teachings not learned before from another.
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no old age and death? When what ceases do old age and death cease?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘jātiyā kho asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hoti, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When rebirth doesn’t exist there’s no old age and death. When rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati jāti na hoti …pe…
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no rebirth? …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
consciousness …

segs.p: saṅkhārā na honti, kissa nirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist are there no choices? When what ceases do choices cease?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘avijjāya kho asati saṅkhārā na honti, avijjānirodhā saṅkhāranirodho’ti.
segs.e: ‘When ignorance doesn’t exist there are no choices. When ignorance ceases, choices cease.’
And so, when ignorance ceases, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

segs.p: ‘Nirodho, nirodho’ti kho me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṁ udapādi, ñāṇaṁ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādī”ti.
segs.e: ‘Cessation, cessation.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in me regarding teachings not learned before from another.”

2. Fuel
Fuel
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme …
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. …

segs.p: “cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four fuels maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.
What four?

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṁ catutthaṁ.
segs.e: Edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: These are the four fuels that maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.

segs.p: Ime, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā kiṁnidānā kiṁsamudayā kiṁjātikā kiṁpabhavā?
segs.e: What is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of these four fuels?

segs.p: Ime cattāro āhārā taṇhānidānā taṇhāsamudayā taṇhājātikā taṇhāpabhavā.
segs.e: Craving.

segs.p: Taṇhā cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kiṁnidānā kiṁsamudayā kiṁjātikā kiṁpabhavā?
segs.e: And what is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of craving?
Feeling.

segs.p: Vedanā cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kiṁnidānā kiṁsamudayā kiṁjātikā kiṁpabhavā?
segs.e: And what is the source of feeling?
Contact.

segs.p: Phasso cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kiṁnidāno kiṁsamudayo kiṁjātiko kiṁpabhavo?
segs.e: And what is the source of contact?
The six sense fields.

segs.p: Saḷāyatanañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, kiṁnidānaṁ kiṁsamudayaṁ kiṁjātikaṁ kiṁpabhavaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the source of the six sense fields?
Name and form.

segs.p: Nāmarūpañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, kiṁnidānaṁ kiṁsamudayaṁ kiṁjātikaṁ kiṁpabhavaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the source of name and form?
Consciousness.

segs.p: Viññāṇañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, kiṁnidānaṁ kiṁsamudayaṁ kiṁjātikaṁ kiṁpabhavaṁ?
segs.e: And what is the source of consciousness?
Choices.

segs.p: Saṅkhārā cime, bhikkhave, kiṁnidānā kiṁsamudayā kiṁjātikā kiṁpabhavā?
segs.e: And what is the source of choices?
Ignorance.
And so, mendicants, ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

2. Fuel
Phagguna of the Top-Knot
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four fuels maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.
What four?

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṁ catutthaṁ.
segs.e: Edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the four fuels that maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those that are about to be born.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā moḷiyaphagguno bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Phagguna of the Top-Knot said to the Buddha,
“But sir, who consumes consciousness as fuel?”
“That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.
“I don’t speak of one who consumes.
If I were to speak of one who consumes, then it would be cogent to ask
who consumes.
But I don’t speak like that.

segs.p: Evaṁ maṁ avadantaṁ yo evaṁ puccheyya:
segs.e: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

segs.p: ‘kissa nu kho, bhante, viññāṇāhāro’ti, esa kallo pañho.
segs.e: ‘For what is consciousness the fuel?’
And a cogent answer to this would be:

segs.p: ‘viññāṇāhāro āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā paccayo, tasmiṁ bhūte sati saḷāyatanaṁ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Consciousness as fuel is a requirement for regeneration into a new state of existence in the future. When the being is present, there are the six sense fields. The six sense fields are requirements for contact.’”
“But sir, who contacts?”
“That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.
“I don’t speak of one who contacts.
If I were to speak of one who contacts, then it would be cogent to ask
who contacts.
But I don’t speak like that.

segs.p: Evaṁ maṁ avadantaṁ yo evaṁ puccheyya:
segs.e: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

segs.p: ‘kiṁpaccayā nu kho, bhante, phasso’ti, esa kallo pañho.
segs.e: ‘What is a requirement for contact?’
And a cogent answer to this would be:
‘The six sense fields are requirements for contact. Contact is a requirement for feeling.’”
“But sir, who feels?”
“That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.
“I don’t speak of one who feels.
If I were to speak of one who feels, then it would be cogent to ask
who feels.
But I don’t speak like that.

segs.p: Evaṁ maṁ avadantaṁ yo evaṁ puccheyya:
segs.e: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

segs.p: ‘kiṁpaccayā nu kho, bhante, vedanā’ti, esa kallo pañho.
segs.e: ‘What is a requirement for feeling?’
And a cogent answer to this would be:
‘Contact is a requirement for feeling. Feeling is a requirement for craving.’”
“But sir, who craves?”
“That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.
“I don’t speak of one who craves.
If I were to speak of one who craves, then it would be cogent to ask
who craves.
But I don’t speak like that.

segs.p: Evaṁ maṁ avadantaṁ yo evaṁ puccheyya:
segs.e: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

segs.p: ‘kiṁpaccayā nu kho, bhante, taṇhā’ti, esa kallo pañho.
segs.e: ‘What is a requirement for craving?’
And a cogent answer to this would be:
‘Feeling is a requirement for craving. Craving is a requirement for grasping.’”
“But sir, who grasps?”
“That’s not a cogent question,” said the Buddha.
“I don’t speak of one who grasps.
If I were to speak of one who grasps, then it would be cogent to ask
who grasps.
But I don’t speak like that.

segs.p: Evaṁ maṁ avadantaṁ yo evaṁ puccheyya:
segs.e: Hence it would be cogent to ask:

segs.p: ‘kiṁpaccayā nu kho, bhante, upādānan’ti, esa kallo pañho.
segs.e: ‘What is a requirement for grasping?’
And a cogent answer to this would be:
‘Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.’ …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Channaṁ tveva, phagguna, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā phassanirodho;
segs.e: When the six fields of contact fade away and cease with no residue left behind, contact ceases.
When contact ceases, feeling ceases.
When feeling ceases, craving ceases.
When craving ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

Ascetics and Brahmins
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṁ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṁ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṁ nappajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānanti;
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.
They don’t understand rebirth …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
consciousness …

segs.p: saṅkhāre nappajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ nappajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānanti,
segs.e: They don’t understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

segs.p: na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā; na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṁ vā brahmaññatthaṁ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.
segs.e: I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā jarāmaraṇaṁ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṁ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṁ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti;
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who do understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.
They understand rebirth …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
consciousness …

segs.p: saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti,
segs.e: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

segs.p: te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā; te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.
segs.e: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ime dhamme pajānanti, imesaṁ dhammānaṁ samudayaṁ pajānanti, imesaṁ dhammānaṁ nirodhaṁ pajānanti, imesaṁ dhammānaṁ nirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti, katame dhamme pajānanti, katamesaṁ dhammānaṁ samudayaṁ pajānanti, katamesaṁ dhammānaṁ nirodhaṁ pajānanti, katamesaṁ dhammānaṁ nirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti?

segs.p: Jarāmaraṇaṁ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇasamudayaṁ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhaṁ pajānanti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti;

segs.p: saṅkhāre pajānanti, saṅkhārasamudayaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhaṁ pajānanti, saṅkhāranirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti.
segs.e: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

segs.p: Ime dhamme pajānanti, imesaṁ dhammānaṁ samudayaṁ pajānanti, imesaṁ dhammānaṁ nirodhaṁ pajānanti, imesaṁ dhammānaṁ nirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānanti.
segs.e: They understand these things, their origin, their cessation, and the practice that leads to their cessation.

segs.p: Te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā, brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā. Te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.
segs.e: I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

2. Fuel
Kaccānagotta
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā kaccānagotto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā kaccānagotto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Kaccānagotta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘right view’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sammādiṭṭhi hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is right view defined?”
“Kaccāna, this world mostly relies on the duality of existence and non-existence.

segs.p: Lokasamudayaṁ kho, kaccāna, yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato yā loke natthitā sā na hoti.
segs.e: But for one who truly sees the origin of the world with right understanding, the concept of non-existence regarding the world does not occur.

segs.p: Lokanirodhaṁ kho, kaccāna, yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passato yā loke atthitā sā na hoti.
segs.e: And for one who truly sees the cessation of the world with right understanding, the concept of existence regarding the world does not occur.
This world is for the most part shackled by getting involved, grasping, and insisting.

segs.p: Tañcāyaṁ upayupādānaṁ cetaso adhiṭṭhānaṁ abhinivesānusayaṁ na upeti na upādiyati nādhiṭṭhāti: ‘attā me’ti.
segs.e: But if, when it comes to this getting involved & grasping, mental fixation, and insistence & underlying tendency, they are not attracted, do not grasp, and do not fixate on the thought, “my self”,

segs.p: ‘Dukkhameva uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, dukkhaṁ nirujjhamānaṁ nirujjhatī’ti na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati aparapaccayā ñāṇamevassa ettha hoti.
segs.e: they’ll have no doubt or uncertainty that what arises is just suffering arising, and what ceases is just suffering ceasing. Their knowledge of this is independent of others.
This is how right view is defined.
‘All exists’: this is one extreme.
‘All does not exist’: this is the second extreme.

segs.p: Ete te, kaccāna, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

A Dhamma Speaker
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of a ‘Dhamma speaker’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhammakathiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a Dhamma speaker defined?”

segs.p: “Jarāmaraṇassa ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: “If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding old age and death, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Jarāmaraṇassa ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding old age and death, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Jarāmaraṇassa ce bhikkhu nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādāvimutto hoti, ‘diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they’re freed by not grasping, by disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding old age and death, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who has attained extinguishment in this very life’.

segs.p: avijjāya ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, ‘dhammakathiko bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding ignorance, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Avijjāya ce bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, ‘dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhū’ti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding ignorance, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

2. Fuel
With Kassapa, the Naked Ascetic
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.

segs.p: Addasā kho acelo kassapo bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: The naked ascetic Kassapa saw the Buddha coming off in the distance.

segs.p: Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: He went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho acelo kassapo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he stood to one side and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “puccheyyāma mayaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ kañcideva desaṁ, sace no bhavaṁ gotamo okāsaṁ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti.
segs.e: “I’d like to ask the worthy Gotama about a certain point, if you’d take the time to answer.”
“Kassapa, it’s the wrong time for questions.
We’ve entered an inhabited area.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho acelo kassapo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: A second time,

segs.p: “puccheyyāma mayaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ kañcideva desaṁ, sace no bhavaṁ gotamo okāsaṁ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti.

segs.e: and a third time, Kassapa spoke to the Buddha and the Buddha replied.

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, acelo kassapo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, Kassapa said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “na kho pana mayaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ bahudeva pucchitukāmā”ti.
segs.e: “I don’t want to ask much.”
“Ask what you wish, Kassapa.”
“Well, worthy Gotama, is suffering made by oneself?”
“Not so, Kassapa,” said the Buddha.
“Then is suffering made by another?”
“Not so, Kassapa,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca dukkhan’ti?
segs.e: “Well, is suffering made by both oneself and another?”
“Not so, Kassapa,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ dukkhan’ti?
segs.e: “Then does suffering arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another?”
“Not so, Kassapa,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi dukkhan’ti?
segs.e: “Well, is there no such thing as suffering?”
“It’s not that there’s no such thing as suffering.
Suffering is real.”

segs.p: ‘Tena hi bhavaṁ gotamo dukkhaṁ na jānāti, na passatī’ti.
segs.e: “Then does the worthy Gotama not know or see suffering?”

segs.p: ‘Na khvāhaṁ, kassapa, dukkhaṁ na jānāmi, na passāmi.
segs.e: “It’s not that I don’t know or see suffering.
I do know suffering,
I do see suffering.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘sayaṅkataṁ dukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, kassapā’ti vadesi.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, when asked these questions, you say ‘not so’.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, paraṅkataṁ dukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, kassapā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca dukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, kassapā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ dukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, kassapā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi dukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho, kassapa, natthi dukkhaṁ, atthi kho, kassapa, dukkhan’ti vadesi.
segs.e: Yet you say that there is such a thing as suffering.

segs.p: ‘Tena hi bhavaṁ gotamo dukkhaṁ na jānāti na passatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṁ, kassapa, dukkhaṁ na jānāmi na passāmi.

segs.e: And you say that you do know suffering,
and you do see suffering.

segs.p: Ācikkhatu ca me, bhante, bhagavā dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: Sir, let the Blessed One explain suffering to me!

segs.p: Desetu ca me, bhante, bhagavā dukkhan”ti.
segs.e: Let the Blessed One teach me about suffering!”

segs.p: “‘So karoti so paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti kho, kassapa, ādito sato ‘sayaṅkataṁ dukkhan’ti iti vadaṁ sassataṁ etaṁ pareti.
segs.e: “Suppose that he who does the deed and he who experiences the result are one and the same. Then for one who has existed since the beginning, suffering is made by oneself. In speaking like this, one implies this is eternal.

segs.p: ‘Añño karoti añño paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti kho, kassapa, vedanābhitunnassa sato ‘paraṅkataṁ dukkhan’ti iti vadaṁ ucchedaṁ etaṁ pareti.
segs.e: Suppose that he who does the deed is one, and he who experiences the result is another. Then for one stricken by feeling, suffering is made by another. In speaking like this, one implies this is annihilated.

segs.p: Ete te, kassapa, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, acelo kassapo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, Kassapa said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya …pe… ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the Buddha has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Labheyyāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, labheyyaṁ upasampadan”ti.
segs.e: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence?”

segs.p: “Yo kho, kassapa, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṁ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṁ, so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṁ māsānaṁ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya.
segs.e: “Kassapa, if someone formerly ordained in another sect wishes to take the going forth, the ordination in this teaching and training, they must spend four months on probation. When four months have passed, if the mendicants are satisfied, they’ll give the going forth, the ordination into monkhood.
However, I have recognized individual differences.”

segs.p: “Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṁ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṁ, cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṁ māsānaṁ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Ahaṁ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi, catunnaṁ vassānaṁ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, if four months probation are required in such a case, I’ll spend four years on probation. When four years have passed, if the mendicants are satisfied, let them give me the going forth, the ordination into monkhood.”

segs.p: Alattha kho acelo kassapo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And the naked ascetic Kassapa received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno ca panāyasmā kassapo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Kassapa, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā kassapo arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Kassapa became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Atha kho timbaruko paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Timbaruka went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho timbaruko paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṅkataṁ sukhadukkhanti?

segs.p: Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, paraṅkataṁ sukhadukkhanti?

segs.p: Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca sukhadukkhanti?

segs.p: Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi sukhadukkhanti?

segs.p: Tena hi bhavaṁ gotamo sukhadukkhaṁ na jānāti, na passatīti?

segs.p: Na khvāhaṁ, timbaruka, sukhadukkhaṁ na jānāmi, na passāmi.
segs.e: “It’s not that I don’t know or see pleasure and pain.
I do know pleasure and pain,

segs.p: “‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṅkataṁ sukhadukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, timbarukā’ti vadesi.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, when asked these questions, you say ‘not so’.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, paraṅkataṁ sukhadukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, timbarukā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca sukhadukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, timbarukā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ sukhadukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, timbarukā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, natthi sukhadukkhan’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho, timbaruka, natthi sukhadukkhaṁ;
segs.e: Yet you say that there is such a thing as pleasure and pain.

segs.p: ‘Tena hi bhavaṁ gotamo sukhadukkhaṁ na jānāti, na passatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na khvāhaṁ, timbaruka, sukhadukkhaṁ na jānāmi, na passāmi.

segs.e: And you say that you do know pleasure and pain,
and you do see pleasure and pain.

segs.p: Ācikkhatu ca me bhavaṁ gotamo sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: Sir, explain pleasure and pain to me!

segs.p: Desetu ca me bhavaṁ gotamo sukhadukkhan”ti.
segs.e: Teach me about pleasure and pain!”

segs.p: “‘Sā vedanā, so vedayatī’ti kho, timbaruka, ādito sato ‘sayaṅkataṁ sukhadukkhan’ti evampāhaṁ na vadāmi.
segs.e: “Suppose that the feeling and the one who feels it are one and the same. Then for one who has existed since the beginning, pleasure and pain is made by oneself. I don’t say this.

segs.p: ‘Aññā vedanā, añño vedayatī’ti kho, timbaruka, vedanābhitunnassa sato ‘paraṅkataṁ sukhadukkhan’ti evampāhaṁ na vadāmi.
segs.e: Suppose that the feeling is one thing and the one who feels it is another. Then for one stricken by feeling, pleasure and pain is made by another. I don’t say this.

segs.p: Ete te, timbaruka, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, timbaruko paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the wanderer Timbaruka said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

2. Fuel
The Astute and the Foolish
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Avijjānīvaraṇassa, bhikkhave, bālassa taṇhāya sampayuttassa evamayaṁ kāyo samudāgato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, for a fool shrouded by ignorance and coupled to craving, this body has been produced.

segs.p: Iti ayañceva kāyo bahiddhā ca nāmarūpaṁ, itthetaṁ dvayaṁ, dvayaṁ paṭicca phasso saḷevāyatanāni, yehi phuṭṭho bālo sukhadukkhaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: So there is this duality: this body and external name and form. Contact depends on this duality. When contacted through one or other of the six sense fields, the fool experiences pleasure and pain.

segs.p: Avijjānīvaraṇassa, bhikkhave, paṇḍitassa taṇhāya sampayuttassa evamayaṁ kāyo samudāgato.
segs.e: For an astute person shrouded by ignorance and coupled to craving, this body has been produced.

segs.p: Iti ayañceva kāyo bahiddhā ca nāmarūpaṁ, itthetaṁ dvayaṁ, dvayaṁ paṭicca phasso saḷevāyatanāni, yehi phuṭṭho paṇḍito sukhadukkhaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: So there is this duality: this body and external name and form. Contact depends on this duality. When contacted through one or other of the six sense fields, the astute person experiences pleasure and pain.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, ko viseso ko adhippayāso kiṁ nānākaraṇaṁ paṇḍitassa bālenā”ti?
segs.e: What, then, is the difference between the foolish and the astute?”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā, bhagavaṁnettikā, bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṁyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Yāya ca, bhikkhave, avijjāya nivutassa bālassa yāya ca taṇhāya sampayuttassa ayaṁ kāyo samudāgato, sā ceva avijjā bālassa appahīnā sā ca taṇhā aparikkhīṇā.
segs.e: “For a fool shrouded by ignorance and coupled to craving, this body has been produced. But the fool has not given up that ignorance or finished that craving.
Why is that?

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, bālo acari brahmacariyaṁ sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: The fool has not completed the spiritual journey for the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: Tasmā bālo kāyassa bhedā kāyūpago hoti,
segs.e: Therefore, when their body breaks up, the fool passes on to another body.

segs.p: so kāyūpago samāno na parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
segs.e: When they have passed on to another body, they’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
They’re not freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Yāya ca, bhikkhave, avijjāya nivutassa paṇḍitassa yāya ca taṇhāya sampayuttassa ayaṁ kāyo samudāgato, sā ceva avijjā paṇḍitassa pahīnā, sā ca taṇhā parikkhīṇā.
segs.e: For an astute person shrouded by ignorance and coupled to craving, this body has been produced. But the astute person has given up that ignorance and finished that craving.
Why is that?

segs.p: Acari, bhikkhave, paṇḍito brahmacariyaṁ sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: The astute person has completed the spiritual journey for the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: Tasmā paṇḍito kāyassa bhedā na kāyūpago hoti.
segs.e: Therefore, when their body breaks up, the astute person does not pass on to another body.

segs.p: So akāyūpago samāno parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
segs.e: Not passing on to another body, they’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
They’re freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso, ayaṁ adhippayāso, idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ paṇḍitassa bālena yadidaṁ brahmacariyavāso”ti.
segs.e: This is the difference here between the foolish and the astute, that is, leading the spiritual life.”
Linked Discourses 12.20
2. Fuel
Conditions
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Paṭiccasamuppādañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi paṭiccasamuppanne ca dhamme.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you dependent origination and dependently originated phenomena.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what is dependent origination?
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.

segs.p: Uppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ, ṭhitāva sā dhātu dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā idappaccayatā.
segs.e: Whether Realized Ones arise or not, this law of nature persists, this regularity of natural principles, this surety of natural principles, specific conditionality.
A Realized One awakens to this and comprehends it,

segs.p: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññāpeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti.
segs.e: then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and discloses it.
‘Look,’ he says,
‘Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth …
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence …
Craving is a requirement for grasping …
Feeling is a requirement for craving …
Contact is a requirement for feeling …
The six sense fields are requirements for contact …
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields …
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form …
Choices are a requirement for consciousness …
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

segs.p: uppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ, ṭhitāva sā dhātu dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā idappaccayatā.
segs.e: Whether Realized Ones arise or not, this law of nature persists, this regularity of natural principles, this surety of natural principles, specific conditionality.
A Realized One awakens to this and comprehends it,

segs.p: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññāpeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti.
segs.e: then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and discloses it.
‘Look,’ he says,
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.’

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, yā tatra tathatā avitathatā anaññathatā idappaccayatā—
segs.e: So the fact that this is real, not unreal, not otherwise; the specific conditionality of it:
this is called dependent origination.
And what are the dependently originated phenomena?

segs.p: Jarāmaraṇaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ khayadhammaṁ vayadhammaṁ virāgadhammaṁ nirodhadhammaṁ.
segs.e: Old age and death are impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.

segs.p: Jāti, bhikkhave, aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā.
segs.e: Rebirth …

segs.p: Bhavo, bhikkhave, anicco saṅkhato paṭiccasamuppanno khayadhammo vayadhammo virāgadhammo nirodhadhammo.
segs.e: Continued existence …
Grasping …
Craving …
Feeling …
Contact …
The six sense fields …
Name and form …
Consciousness …
Choices …

segs.p: avijjā, bhikkhave, aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā.
segs.e: Ignorance is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, liable to end, vanish, fade away, and cease.
These are called the dependently originated phenomena.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa ‘ayañca paṭiccasamuppādo, ime ca paṭiccasamuppannā dhammā’ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti, so vata pubbantaṁ vā paṭidhāvissati:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has clearly seen with right wisdom this dependent origination and these dependently originated phenomena as they are, it will be quite impossible for them to turn back to the first beginning, thinking:

segs.p: ‘ahosiṁ nu kho ahaṁ atītamaddhānaṁ, nanu kho ahosiṁ atītamaddhānaṁ, kiṁ nu kho ahosiṁ atītamaddhānaṁ, kathaṁ nu kho ahosiṁ atītamaddhānaṁ, kiṁ hutvā kiṁ ahosiṁ nu kho ahaṁ atītamaddhānan’ti;
segs.e: ‘Did I exist in the past? Did I not exist in the past? What was I in the past? How was I in the past? After being what, what did I become in the past?’
Or to turn forward to the final end, thinking:

segs.p: ‘bhavissāmi nu kho ahaṁ anāgatamaddhānaṁ, nanu kho bhavissāmi anāgatamaddhānaṁ, kiṁ nu kho bhavissāmi anāgatamaddhānaṁ, kathaṁ nu kho bhavissāmi anāgatamaddhānaṁ, kiṁ hutvā kiṁ bhavissāmi nu kho ahaṁ anāgatamaddhānan’ti;
segs.e: ‘Will I exist in the future? Will I not exist in the future? What will I be in the future? How will I be in the future? After being what, what will I become in the future?’

segs.p: etarahi vā paccuppannaṁ addhānaṁ ajjhattaṁ kathaṅkathī bhavissati:
segs.e: Or to be undecided about the present, thinking:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ nu khosmi, no nu khosmi, kiṁ nu khosmi, kathaṁ nu khosmi, ayaṁ nu kho satto kuto āgato, so kuhiṁ gamissatī’ti—
segs.e: ‘Am I? Am I not? What am I? How am I? This sentient being—where did it come from? And where will it go?’
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hi, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa ayañca paṭiccasamuppādo ime ca paṭiccasamuppannā dhammā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā”ti.
segs.e: Because that noble disciple has clearly seen with right wisdom this dependent origination and these dependently originated phenomena as they are.”
Linked Discourses 12.21
3. The Ten Powers
The Ten Powers
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Dasabalasamannāgato, bhikkhave, tathāgato catūhi ca vesārajjehi samannāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti—
segs.e: “Mendicants, a Realized One has ten powers and four kinds of self-assurance. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

segs.p: iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

segs.p: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the disappearance of feeling.

segs.p: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the disappearance of perception.

segs.p: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the disappearance of choices.

segs.p: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo.
segs.e: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.

segs.p: Iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati.
segs.e: So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: Imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
Linked Discourses 12.22
3. The Ten Powers
The Ten Powers (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Dasabalasamannāgato, bhikkhave, tathāgato catūhi ca vesārajjehi samannāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti:
segs.e: “Mendicants, a Realized One has ten powers and four kinds of self-assurance. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

segs.p: ‘iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

segs.p: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the disappearance of feeling.

segs.p: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the disappearance of perception.

segs.p: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the disappearance of choices.

segs.p: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo.
segs.e: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.

segs.p: Iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
segs.e: So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

segs.p: Evaṁ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko.
segs.e: The teaching well-explained thus by me is clarified, revealed, illuminated, and stripped of patchwork.

segs.p: Evaṁ svākkhāte kho, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike alameva saddhāpabbajitena kulaputtena vīriyaṁ ārabhituṁ:
segs.e: In this teaching thus well-explained, it is quite enough for a gentleman who has gone forth out of faith to rouse up energy.

segs.p: ‘kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upassussatu maṁsalohitaṁ. Yaṁ taṁ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṁ, na taṁ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Gladly, let only skin, sinews, and tendons remain! Let the flesh and blood waste away in my body! I will not stop trying until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.’

segs.p: Dukkhaṁ, bhikkhave, kusīto viharati vokiṇṇo pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi, mahantañca sadatthaṁ parihāpeti.
segs.e: A lazy person lives in suffering, mixed up with bad, unskillful qualities, neglecting their heart’s great goal.

segs.p: Āraddhavīriyo ca kho, bhikkhave, sukhaṁ viharati pavivitto pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi, mahantañca sadatthaṁ paripūreti.
segs.e: But an energetic person lives happily, secluded from bad, unskillful qualities, fulfilling their heart’s great goal.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, hīnena aggassa patti hoti.
segs.e: The best isn’t reached by the worst.

segs.p: Aggena ca kho, bhikkhave, aggassa patti hoti.
segs.e: The best is reached by the best.
This spiritual life is the cream, mendicants, and the Teacher is before you.

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, vīriyaṁ ārabhatha appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: So you should rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized, thinking:

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ no ayaṁ amhākaṁ pabbajjā avañjhā bhavissati saphalā saudrayā.
segs.e: ‘In this way our going forth will not be barren, but will be fruitful and fertile.

segs.p: Yesañca mayaṁ paribhuñjāma cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ tesaṁ te kārā amhesu mahapphalā bhavissanti mahānisaṁsā’ti—
segs.e: And the services of those whose robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick we enjoy shall be very fruitful and beneficial for them.’
That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Attatthaṁ vā hi, bhikkhave, sampassamānena alameva appamādena sampādetuṁ;
segs.e: Considering what is good for yourself, mendicants, is quite enough for you to persist with diligence.

segs.p: paratthaṁ vā hi, bhikkhave, sampassamānena alameva appamādena sampādetuṁ;
segs.e: Considering what is good for others is quite enough for you to persist with diligence.

segs.p: ubhayatthaṁ vā hi, bhikkhave, sampassamānena alameva appamādena sampādetun”ti.
segs.e: Considering what is good for both is quite enough for you to persist with diligence.”
Linked Discourses 12.23
3. The Ten Powers
Vital Conditions
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Jānato ahaṁ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṁ khayaṁ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I say that the ending of defilements is for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or see.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṁ passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti?
segs.e: For one who knows and sees what?

segs.p: Iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo,
segs.e: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.
Such is feeling …
Such is perception …
Such are choices …

segs.p: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamoti.
segs.e: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṁ passato āsavānaṁ khayo hoti.
segs.e: The ending of the defilements is for one who knows and sees this.

segs.p: Yampissa taṁ, bhikkhave, khayasmiṁ khaye ñāṇaṁ, tampi saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that this knowledge of ending has a vital condition, it doesn’t lack a vital condition.

segs.p: Kā ca, bhikkhave, khaye ñāṇassa upanisā?
segs.e: And what is it?
You should say: ‘Freedom.’

segs.p: Vimuttimpāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that freedom has a vital condition, it doesn’t lack a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Dispassion.’

segs.p: Virāgampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that dispassion has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Disillusionment.’

segs.p: Nibbidampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that disillusionment has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Truly knowing and seeing.’

segs.p: Yathābhūtañāṇadassanampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that truly knowing and seeing has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Immersion.’

segs.p: Samādhimpāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that immersion has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Bliss.’

segs.p: Sukhampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that bliss has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Tranquility.’

segs.p: Passaddhimpāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that tranquility has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Rapture.’

segs.p: Pītimpāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that rapture has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Joy.’

segs.p: Pāmojjampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that joy has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Faith.’

segs.p: Saddhampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that faith has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Suffering.’

segs.p: Dukkhampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that suffering has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Rebirth.’

segs.p: Jātimpāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that rebirth has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Continued existence.’

segs.p: Bhavampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that continued existence has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Grasping.’

segs.p: Upādānampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that grasping has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Craving.’

segs.p: Taṇhampāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanisaṁ vadāmi, no anupanisaṁ.
segs.e: I say that craving has a vital condition.
And what is it?
You should say: ‘Feeling.’ …
You should say: ‘Contact.’ …
You should say: ‘The six sense fields.’ …
You should say: ‘Name and form.’ …
You should say: ‘Consciousness.’ …
You should say: ‘Choices.’ …

segs.p: Saṅkhārepāhaṁ, bhikkhave, saupanise vadāmi, no anupanise.
segs.e: I say that choices have a vital condition, they don’t lack a vital condition.
And what is the vital condition for choices?
You should say: ‘Ignorance.’
So, mendicants: ignorance is the vital condition for choices.
Choices are the vital condition for consciousness.
Consciousness is the vital condition for name and form.
Name and form are the vital conditions for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are the vital conditions for contact.
Contact is the vital condition for feeling.
Feeling is the vital condition for craving.
Craving is the vital condition for grasping.
Grasping is the vital condition for continued existence.
Continued existence is the vital condition for rebirth.
Rebirth is the vital condition for suffering.
Suffering is the vital condition for faith.
Faith is the vital condition for joy.
Joy is the vital condition for rapture.
Rapture is the vital condition for tranquility.
Tranquility is the vital condition for bliss.
Bliss is the vital condition for immersion.
Immersion is the vital condition for truly knowing and seeing.
Truly knowing and seeing is the vital condition for disillusionment.
Disillusionment is the vital condition for dispassion.
Dispassion is the vital condition for freedom.
Freedom is the vital condition for the knowledge of ending.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṁ udakaṁ yathāninnaṁ pavattamānaṁ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti. Pabbatakandarapadarasākhāparipūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti. Kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe paripūrenti. Mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti. Kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti. Mahānadiyo paripūrā mahāsamuddaṁ paripūrenti.
segs.e: It’s like when the heavens rain heavily on a mountain top, and the water flows downhill to fill the hollows, crevices, and creeks. As they become full, they fill up the pools. The pools fill up the lakes, the lakes fill up the streams, and the streams fill up the rivers. And as the rivers become full, they fill up the ocean.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, avijjūpanisā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārūpanisaṁ viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇūpanisaṁ nāmarūpaṁ, nāmarūpūpanisaṁ saḷāyatanaṁ, saḷāyatanūpaniso phasso, phassūpanisā vedanā, vedanūpanisā taṇhā, taṇhūpanisaṁ upādānaṁ, upādānūpaniso bhavo, bhavūpanisā jāti, jātūpanisaṁ dukkhaṁ, dukkhūpanisā saddhā, saddhūpanisaṁ pāmojjaṁ, pāmojjūpanisā pīti, pītūpanisā passaddhi, passaddhūpanisaṁ sukhaṁ, sukhūpaniso samādhi, samādhūpanisaṁ yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ, yathābhūtañāṇadassanūpanisā nibbidā, nibbidūpaniso virāgo, virāgūpanisā vimutti, vimuttūpanisaṁ khaye ñāṇan”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, ignorance is the vital condition for choices. … Freedom is the vital condition for the knowledge of ending.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.

segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The wanderers said to him:

segs.p: “Santāvuso sāriputta, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkataṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, there are ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. Some of them assert that suffering is made by oneself.

segs.p: Santi panāvuso sāriputta, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā paraṅkataṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
segs.e: Some of them assert that suffering is made by another.

segs.p: Santāvuso sāriputta, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca dukkhaṁ paññapenti.

segs.p: Santi panāvuso sāriputta, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kammavādā asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ dukkhaṁ paññapenti.
segs.e: Some of them assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another.

segs.p: Idha, panāvuso sāriputta, samaṇo gotamo kiṁvādī kimakkhāyī?
segs.e: What does the ascetic Gotama say about this? How does he explain it?

segs.p: Kathaṁ byākaramānā ca mayaṁ vuttavādino ceva samaṇassa gotamassa assāma, na ca samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākareyyāma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānupāto gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgaccheyyā”ti?
segs.e: How should we answer so as to repeat what the ascetic Gotama has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should we explain in line with his teaching, with no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”
“Reverends, the Buddha has said that suffering is dependently originated.
Dependent on what?
Dependent on contact.

segs.p: Iti vadaṁ vuttavādī ceva bhagavato assa, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkheyya, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākareyya, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānupāto gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgaccheyya.
