4. Kaḷāra the Aristocrat
Ignorance is a Requirement (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.
“Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: ‘Katamaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, kassa ca panidaṁ jarāmaraṇan’ti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ‘aññaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, aññassa ca panidaṁ jarāmaraṇan’ti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṁ ekatthaṁ byañjanameva nānaṁ.
segs.e: Mendicants, you might say, ‘What are old age and death, and who do they belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Old age and death are one thing, who they belong to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.

segs.p: ‘Taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.
segs.e: If you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

segs.p: ‘Aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.
segs.e: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

segs.p: Ete te, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’
‘What is rebirth …’
‘What is continued existence …’
‘What is grasping …’
‘What is craving …’
‘What is feeling …’
‘What is contact …’
‘What are the six sense fields …’
‘What are name and form …’
‘What is consciousness …’

segs.p: katame saṅkhārā, kassa ca panime saṅkhārāti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ‘aññe saṅkhārā aññassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ti iti vā, bhikkhave, yo vadeyya, ubhayametaṁ ekatthaṁ byañjanameva nānaṁ.
segs.e: You might say, ‘What are choices, and who do they belong to?’ Or you might say, ‘Choices are one thing, who they belong to is another.’ But both of these mean the same thing, only the phrasing differs.

segs.p: ‘Taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.
segs.e: If you have the view that the soul and the body are one and the same, there is no living of the spiritual life.

segs.p: ‘Aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso na hoti.
segs.e: If you have the view that the soul is one thing, the body another, there is no living of the spiritual life.

segs.p: Ete te, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.’

segs.p: Avijjāya tveva, bhikkhave, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici.
segs.e: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, then any twists, ducks, and dodges are given up:

segs.p: ‘Katamaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, kassa ca panidaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, aññassa ca panidaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ’ iti vā, ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ, aññaṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā.
segs.e: ‘What are old age and death, and who do they belong to?’ or ‘old age and death are one thing, who they belong to is another’, or ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’, or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’.

segs.p: Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṁ anuppādadhammāni.
segs.e: These are all cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Avijjāya tveva, bhikkhave, asesavirāganirodhā yānissa tāni visūkāyikāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici.
segs.e: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, then any twists, ducks, and dodges are given up:
‘What is rebirth …’
‘What is continued existence …’
‘What is grasping …’
‘What is craving …’
‘What is feeling …’
‘What is contact …’
‘What are the six sense fields …’
‘What are name and form …’
‘What is consciousness …’

segs.p: ‘katame saṅkhārā, kassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ iti vā, ‘aññe saṅkhārā, aññassa ca panime saṅkhārā’ iti vā; ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā, ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīraṁ’ iti vā.
segs.e: ‘What are choices, and who do they belong to?’ or ‘choices are one thing, who they belong to is another’, or ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’, or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’.

segs.p: Sabbānissa tāni pahīnāni bhavanti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṁ anuppādadhammānī”ti.
segs.e: These are all cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”
Linked Discourses 12.37
4. Kaḷāra the Aristocrat
Not Yours
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, this body doesn’t belong to you or to anyone else.

segs.p: Purāṇamidaṁ, bhikkhave, kammaṁ abhisaṅkhataṁ abhisañcetayitaṁ vedaniyaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: It’s old deeds, and should be seen as produced by choices and intentions, as something to be felt.

segs.p: Tatra kho, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti:
segs.e: A learned noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

segs.p: ‘iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
segs.e: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”
Linked Discourses 12.38
4. Kaḷāra the Aristocrat
Intention
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Yañca, bhikkhave, ceteti yañca pakappeti yañca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, what you intend or plan, and what you have underlying tendencies for become a support for the continuation of consciousness.
When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is established and grows, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā sati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti.
segs.e: When there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: No ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ce pakappeti, atha ce anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: If you don’t intend or plan, but still have underlying tendencies, this becomes a support for the continuation of consciousness.
When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is established and grows, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā sati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti.
segs.e: When there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, no ceva ceteti no ca pakappeti no ca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ na hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: If you don’t intend or plan or have underlying tendencies, this doesn’t become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

segs.p: Ārammaṇe asati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: With no support, consciousness is not established.

segs.p: Tadappatiṭṭhite viññāṇe avirūḷhe āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti na hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, there’s no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbattiyā asati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: When there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, future rebirth, old age, and death cease, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
Linked Discourses 12.39
4. Kaḷāra the Aristocrat
Intention (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Yañca, bhikkhave, ceteti yañca pakappeti yañca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, what you intend or plan, and what you have underlying tendencies for become a support for the continuation of consciousness.
When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nāmarūpassa avakkanti hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling. …
craving …
grasping …
continued existence …
rebirth …
old age and death,
sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: No ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ce pakappeti, atha ce anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: If you don’t intend or plan, but still have underlying tendencies, this becomes a support for the continuation of consciousness.
When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nāmarūpassa avakkanti hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, no ceva ceteti no ca pakappeti no ca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ na hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: If you don’t intend or plan or have underlying tendencies, this doesn’t become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

segs.p: Ārammaṇe asati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: With no support, consciousness is not established.

segs.p: Tadappatiṭṭhite viññāṇe avirūḷhe nāmarūpassa avakkanti na hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, name and form are not conceived.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
Linked Discourses 12.40
4. Kaḷāra the Aristocrat
Intention (3rd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Yañca, bhikkhave, ceteti yañca pakappeti yañca anuseti ārammaṇametaṁ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, what you intend or plan, and what you have underlying tendencies for become a support for the continuation of consciousness.
When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nati hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is established and grows, there is an inclination.
When there is an inclination, there is coming and going.
When there is coming and going, there is passing away and reappearing.

segs.p: Cutūpapāte sati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti.
segs.e: When there is passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: No ce, bhikkhave, ceteti no ce pakappeti atha ce anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: If you don’t intend or plan, but still have underlying tendencies, this becomes a support for the continuation of consciousness.
When this support exists, consciousness becomes established.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe virūḷhe nati hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is established and grows, there is an inclination.
When there is an inclination, there is coming and going.
When there is coming and going, there is passing away and reappearing.

segs.p: Cutūpapāte sati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti.
segs.e: When there is passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death come to be, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, no ceva ceteti no ca pakappeti no ca anuseti, ārammaṇametaṁ na hoti viññāṇassa ṭhitiyā.
segs.e: If you don’t intend or plan or have underlying tendencies, this doesn’t become a support for the continuation of consciousness.

segs.p: Ārammaṇe asati patiṭṭhā viññāṇassa na hoti.
segs.e: With no support, consciousness is not established.

segs.p: Tadappatiṭṭhite viññāṇe avirūḷhe nati na hoti.
segs.e: When consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, there’s no inclination.
When there’s no inclination, there’s no coming and going.
When there’s no coming and going, there’s no passing away and reappearing.

segs.p: Cutūpapāte asati āyatiṁ jāti jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: When there’s no passing away and reappearing, future rebirth, old age, and death cease, as do sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
Linked Discourses 12.41
5. Householders
Fears and Enmities
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Buddha said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:

segs.p: “Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “Householder, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

segs.p: Katamāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti?
segs.e: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati, pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, adinnādāyī adinnādānapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati, adinnādānā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Anyone who steals brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from stealing.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, kāmesumicchācārī kāmesumicchācārapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati, kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Anyone who commits sexual misconduct brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from sexual misconduct.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, musāvādī musāvādapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati, musāvādā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Anyone who lies brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from lying.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. That fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.

segs.p: Imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.
segs.e: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.
What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
They have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’
They have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.
These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

segs.p: Katamo cassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho?
segs.e: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti:
segs.e: A noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

segs.p: ‘iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti;
segs.e: ‘So, when this exists, that comes to be; when this doesn’t exist, that is not.

segs.p: imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: Due to the arising of this, that arises; due to the cessation of this, that ceases.
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’

segs.p: Ayamassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho.
segs.e: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

segs.p: Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

5. Householders
Fears and Enmities (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

segs.p: Katamāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti?
segs.e: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?
Killing living creatures …
stealing …
sexual misconduct …
lying …
consuming intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor …

segs.p: imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.
segs.e: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.
What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?
It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …
the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
and their ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones.
These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

segs.p: Katamo cassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho?
segs.e: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti …pe…
segs.e: A noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself …

segs.p: ayamassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho.
segs.e: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

5. Householders
Suffering
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you the origin and disappearance of suffering.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what, mendicants, is the origin of suffering?

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving. …
This is the origin of suffering.

segs.p: Sotañca paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇaṁ …pe…
segs.e: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …
Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …
Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …
Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

segs.p: manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving. …
This is the origin of suffering.
And what is the disappearance of suffering?

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
This is the disappearance of suffering.

segs.p: Sotañca paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇaṁ …pe…
segs.e: Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …
Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …
Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …
Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

segs.p: manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
This is the disappearance of suffering.”

5. Householders
At Ñātika
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā rahogato paṭisallāno imaṁ dhammapariyāyaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then while the Buddha was in private retreat he spoke this exposition of the teaching:

segs.p: “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: “Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …
Nose consciousness arises dependent on the nose and smells. …
Tongue consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and tastes. …
Body consciousness arises dependent on the body and touches. …

segs.p: manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
Craving is a requirement for grasping. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Eye consciousness arises dependent on the eye and sights. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
Ear consciousness arises dependent on the ear and sounds. …

segs.p: manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṁ. Tiṇṇaṁ saṅgati phasso.
segs.e: Mind consciousness arises dependent on the mind and ideas. The meeting of the three is contact.
Contact is a requirement for feeling.
Feeling is a requirement for craving.
When that craving fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bhagavato upassuti ṭhito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain monk was standing listening in on the Buddha.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ upassuti ṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: The Buddha saw him
and said,
“Monk, did you hear that exposition of the teaching?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Learn that exposition of the teaching,
memorize it,
and remember it.
That exposition of the teaching is beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.”
Linked Discourses 12.46
5. Householders
A Certain Brahmin
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, so karoti so paṭisaṁvedayatī”ti?
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, are he who does the deed and he who experiences the result one and the same?”

segs.p: “‘So karoti so paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti kho, brāhmaṇa, ayameko anto”.
segs.e: “‘He who does the deed and he who experiences the result are one and the same’: this is one extreme, brahmin.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, añño karoti, añño paṭisaṁvedayatī”ti?
segs.e: “Then is he who does the deed one and he who experiences the result another?”

segs.p: “‘Añño karoti, añño paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti kho, brāhmaṇa, ayaṁ dutiyo anto.
segs.e: “‘He who does the deed is one and he who experiences the result is another’: this is the second extreme.

segs.p: Ete te, brāhmaṇa, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the brahmin said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Linked Discourses 12.47

segs.p: Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:

From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

5. Householders
A Cosmologist
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho lokāyatiko brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā …pe…
segs.e: Then a brahmin cosmologist went up to the Buddha …

segs.p: ekamantaṁ nisinno kho lokāyatiko brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side he said to the Buddha:
“Worthy Gotama, does all exist?”
“‘All exists’: this is the oldest cosmology, brahmin.”
“Then does all not exist?”
“‘All does not exist’: this is the second cosmology.”
“Well, is all oneness?”
“‘All is oneness’: this is the third cosmology.”
“Then is all expansiveness?”
“‘All is expansiveness’: this is the fourth cosmology.

segs.p: Ete te, brāhmaṇa, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, lokāyatiko brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, the brahmin cosmologist said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …
From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

5. Householders
A Noble Disciple
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, a learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

segs.p: kismiṁ sati kiṁ hoti, kissuppādā kiṁ uppajjati?
segs.e: ‘When what exists, what is? Due to the arising of what, what arises?

segs.p: Kismiṁ sati saṅkhārā honti, kismiṁ sati viññāṇaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati nāmarūpaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati saḷāyatanaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati phasso hoti, kismiṁ sati vedanā hoti, kismiṁ sati taṇhā hoti, kismiṁ sati upādānaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati bhavo hoti, kismiṁ sati jāti hoti, kismiṁ sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hotī’ti?
segs.e: When what exists do name and form come to be? When what exists do the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death come to be?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sutavato ariyasāvakassa aparappaccayā ñāṇamevettha hoti:
segs.e: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

segs.p: ‘imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati.
segs.e: ‘When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.
When ignorance exists choices come to be.
When choices exist consciousness comes to be.
When consciousness exists name and form come to be.
When name and form exist the six sense fields come to be.
When the six sense fields exist contact comes to be.
When contact exists feeling comes to be.
When feeling exists craving comes to be.
When craving exists grasping comes to be.
When grasping exists continued existence comes to be.
When continued existence exists rebirth comes to be.
When rebirth exists old age and death come to be.’
They understand:
‘That is how this world originates.’

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, sutavato ariyasāvakassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: A learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

segs.p: kismiṁ asati kiṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā kiṁ nirujjhati?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist, what is not? Due to the cessation of what, what ceases?

segs.p: Kismiṁ asati saṅkhārā na honti, kismiṁ asati viññāṇaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati nāmarūpaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati saḷāyatanaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati phasso na hoti, kismiṁ asati vedanā na hoti, kismiṁ asati taṇhā na hoti, kismiṁ asati upādānaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati bhavo na hoti, kismiṁ asati jāti na hoti, kismiṁ asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hotī’ti?
segs.e: When what doesn’t exist do choices not come to be? When what doesn’t exist do name and form not come to be? When what doesn’t exist do the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death not come to be?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sutavato ariyasāvakassa aparappaccayā ñāṇamevettha hoti:
segs.e: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

segs.p: ‘imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: ‘When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases.
When ignorance doesn’t exist choices don’t come to be.
When choices don’t exist consciousness doesn’t come to be.
When consciousness doesn’t exist name and form don’t come to be.
When name and form don’t exist the six sense fields don’t come to be. …
continued existence doesn’t come to be …
rebirth doesn’t come to be …
When rebirth doesn’t exist old age and death don’t come to be.’
They understand:
‘That is how this world ceases.’

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ lokassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako diṭṭhisampanno itipi …pe…
segs.e: A noble disciple comes to truly understand the origin and disappearance of the world. Such a noble disciple is one who is called ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands knocking at the door to freedom from death’.”
Linked Discourses 12.50
5. Householders
A Noble Disciple (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, a learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho kismiṁ sati kiṁ hoti, kissuppādā kiṁ uppajjati?
segs.e: ‘When what exists, what is? Due to the arising of what, what arises?

segs.p: Kismiṁ sati saṅkhārā honti, kismiṁ sati viññāṇaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati nāmarūpaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati saḷāyatanaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati phasso hoti, kismiṁ sati vedanā hoti, kismiṁ sati taṇhā hoti, kismiṁ sati upādānaṁ hoti, kismiṁ sati bhavo hoti, kismiṁ sati jāti hoti, kismiṁ sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hotī’ti?
segs.e: When what exists do choices come to be? When what exists does consciousness come to be? When what exists do name and form … the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death come to be?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sutavato ariyasāvakassa aparappaccayā ñāṇamevettha hoti:
segs.e: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

segs.p: ‘imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati.
segs.e: ‘When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.
When ignorance exists, choices come to be.
When choices exist consciousness comes to be.
When consciousness exists name and form come to be.
When name and form exist the six sense fields come to be.
When the six sense fields exist contact comes to be.
When contact exists feeling comes to be.
When feeling exists craving comes to be.
When craving exists grasping comes to be.
When grasping exists continued existence comes to be.
When continued existence exists rebirth comes to be.
When rebirth exists old age and death come to be.’
They understand:
‘That is how this world originates.’

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, sutavato ariyasāvakassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: A learned noble disciple doesn’t think:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho kismiṁ asati kiṁ na hoti, kissa nirodhā kiṁ nirujjhati?
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist, what is not? Due to the cessation of what, what ceases?

segs.p: Kismiṁ asati saṅkhārā na honti, kismiṁ asati viññāṇaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati nāmarūpaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati saḷāyatanaṁ na hoti, kismiṁ asati phasso na hoti, kismiṁ asati vedanā na hoti, kismiṁ asati taṇhā na hoti …pe…
segs.e: When what doesn’t exist do choices not come to be? When what doesn’t exist does consciousness not come to be? When what doesn’t exist do name and form … the six sense fields … contact … feeling … craving … grasping … continued existence … rebirth … old age and death not come to be?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sutavato ariyasāvakassa aparappaccayā ñāṇamevettha hoti:
segs.e: Rather, a learned noble disciple has only knowledge about this that is independent of others:

segs.p: ‘imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: ‘When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
When ignorance doesn’t exists, choices don’t come to be.
When choices don’t exist consciousness doesn’t come to be.
When consciousness doesn’t exist name and form don’t come to be.
When name and form don’t exist the six sense fields don’t come to be. …
When rebirth doesn’t exist old age and death don’t come to be.’
They understand:
‘That is how this world ceases.’

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṁ lokassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako diṭṭhisampanno itipi, dassanasampanno itipi, āgato imaṁ saddhammaṁ itipi, passati imaṁ saddhammaṁ itipi, sekkhena ñāṇena samannāgato itipi, sekkhāya vijjāya samannāgato itipi, dhammasotaṁ samāpanno itipi, ariyo nibbedhikapañño itipi, amatadvāraṁ āhacca tiṭṭhati itipī”ti.
segs.e: A noble disciple comes to truly understand the origin and disappearance of the world. Such a noble disciple is one who is called ‘one accomplished in view’, ‘one accomplished in vision’, ‘one who has come to the true teaching’, ‘one who sees this true teaching’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s insight’, ‘one endowed with a trainee’s knowledge’, ‘one who has entered the stream of the teaching’, ‘a noble one with penetrative wisdom’, and also ‘one who stands pressing against the door to freedom from death’.”
Linked Discourses 12.51
6. Suffering
An Inquiry
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Kittāvatā nu kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parivīmaṁsamāno parivīmaṁseyya sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāyā”ti?
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant is inquiring, how do you define when they are inquiring for the complete ending of suffering?”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṁnettikā bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṁyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, take a mendicant who makes an inquiry:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho idaṁ anekavidhaṁ nānappakārakaṁ dukkhaṁ loke uppajjati jarāmaraṇaṁ;
segs.e: ‘The suffering that arises in the world starting with old age and death takes many and diverse forms.

segs.p: idaṁ nu kho dukkhaṁ kiṁnidānaṁ kiṁsamudayaṁ kiṁjātikaṁ kiṁpabhavaṁ?
segs.e: What is the source, origin, birthplace, and inception of this suffering?

segs.p: Kismiṁ sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, kismiṁ asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hotī’ti?
segs.e: When what exists do old age and death come to be? When what does not exist do old age and death not come to be?’
While making an inquiry they understand:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho idaṁ anekavidhaṁ nānappakārakaṁ dukkhaṁ loke uppajjati jarāmaraṇaṁ, idaṁ kho dukkhaṁ jātinidānaṁ jātisamudayaṁ jātijātikaṁ jātippabhavaṁ.
segs.e: ‘The suffering that arises in the world starting with old age and death takes many and diverse forms. The source of this suffering is rebirth.

segs.p: Jātiyā sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, jātiyā asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hotī’ti.
segs.e: When rebirth exists, old age and death come to be. When rebirth doesn’t exist, old age and death don’t come to be.’

segs.p: So jarāmaraṇañca pajānāti, jarāmaraṇasamudayañca pajānāti, jarāmaraṇanirodhañca pajānāti, yā ca jarāmaraṇanirodhasāruppagāminī paṭipadā tañca pajānāti, tathā paṭipanno ca hoti anudhammacārī;
segs.e: They understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the fitting practice for their cessation. And they practice in line with that path.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya paṭipanno jarāmaraṇanirodhāya.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of old age and death.
Then they inquire further:

segs.p: ‘jāti panāyaṁ kiṁnidānā kiṁsamudayā kiṁjātikā kiṁpabhavā, kismiṁ sati jāti hoti, kismiṁ asati jāti na hotī’ti?
segs.e: ‘But what is the source of this rebirth? When what exists does rebirth come to be? And when what does not exist does rebirth not come to be?’
While making an inquiry they understand:
‘Continued existence is the source of rebirth.

segs.p: bhave sati jāti hoti, bhave asati jāti na hotī’ti.
segs.e: When continued existence exists, rebirth comes to be. When continued existence does not exist, rebirth doesn’t come to be.’

segs.p: So jātiñca pajānāti, jātisamudayañca pajānāti, jātinirodhañca pajānāti, yā ca jātinirodhasāruppagāminī paṭipadā tañca pajānāti, tathā paṭipanno ca hoti anudhammacārī;
segs.e: They understand rebirth, its origin, its cessation, and the fitting practice for its cessation. And they practice in line with that path.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya paṭipanno jātinirodhāya.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of rebirth.
Then they inquire further:
‘But what is the source of this continued existence? …’ …
‘But what is the source of this grasping? …’ …
‘But what is the source of this craving? …’ …
‘But what is the source of this feeling? …’ …
‘But what is the source of this contact? …’ …
‘But what is the source of these six sense fields? …’ …
‘But what is the source of this name and form? …’ …
‘But what is the source of this consciousness? …’ …

segs.p: saṅkhārā panime kiṁnidānā kiṁsamudayā kiṁjātikā kiṁpabhavā;
segs.e: ‘But what is the source of these choices?

segs.p: kismiṁ sati saṅkhārā honti, kismiṁ asati saṅkhārā na hontī’ti?
segs.e: When what exists do choices come to be? When what does not exist do choices not come to be?’
While making an inquiry they understand:
‘Ignorance is the source of choices.

segs.p: avijjāya sati saṅkhārā honti, avijjāya asati saṅkhārā na hontī’ti.
segs.e: When ignorance exists, choices come to be. When ignorance does not exist, choices don’t come to be.’

segs.p: So saṅkhāre ca pajānāti, saṅkhārasamudayañca pajānāti, saṅkhāranirodhañca pajānāti, yā ca saṅkhāranirodhasāruppagāminī paṭipadā tañca pajānāti, tathā paṭipanno ca hoti anudhammacārī;
segs.e: They understand choices, their origin, their cessation, and the fitting practice for their cessation. And they practice in line with that path.

segs.p: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya paṭipanno saṅkhāranirodhāya.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of choices.

segs.p: Avijjāgato yaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalo puññañce saṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, puññūpagaṁ hoti viññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: If an ignoramus makes a good choice, consciousness passes on by means of goodness.

segs.p: Apuññañce saṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, apuññūpagaṁ hoti viññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: If they make a bad choice, consciousness passes on by means of badness.

segs.p: Āneñjañce saṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti āneñjūpagaṁ hoti viññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: If they make an imperturbable choice, consciousness passes on by means of imperturbability.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjā pahīnā hoti vijjā uppannā, so avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā neva puññābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti na apuññābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti na āneñjābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti.
segs.e: When a mendicant has given up ignorance and given rise to knowledge, with the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge they don’t make a good choice, a bad choice, or an imperturbable choice.

segs.p: Anabhisaṅkharonto anabhisañcetayanto na kiñci loke upādiyati;
segs.e: Not choosing or intending, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.

segs.p: anupādiyaṁ na paritassati, aparitassaṁ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati.
segs.e: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: So sukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, sā aniccāti pajānāti, anajjhositāti pajānāti, anabhinanditāti pajānāti.
segs.e: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t take pleasure in it.

segs.p: Dukkhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, sā aniccāti pajānāti, anajjhositāti pajānāti, anabhinanditāti pajānāti.
segs.e: If they feel a painful feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t take pleasure in it.

segs.p: Adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, sā aniccāti pajānāti, anajjhositāti pajānāti, anabhinanditāti pajānāti.
segs.e: If they feel a neutral feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t take pleasure in it.

segs.p: So sukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaṁyutto naṁ vedayati.
segs.e: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they feel it detached.

segs.p: Dukkhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaṁyutto naṁ vedayati.
segs.e: If they feel a painful feeling, they feel it detached.

segs.p: Adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaṁyutto naṁ vedayati.
segs.e: If they feel a neutral feeling, they feel it detached.

segs.p: So kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmīti pajānāti, jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmīti pajānāti.
segs.e: Feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissanti, sarīrāni avasissantīti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life has come to an end, everything that’s felt, since I no longer take pleasure in it, will become cool right here. Only bodily remains will be left.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso kumbhakārapākā uṇhaṁ kumbhaṁ uddharitvā same bhūmibhāge paṭisisseyya.
segs.e: Suppose a person were to remove a hot clay pot from a potter’s kiln and place it down on level ground.

segs.p: Tatra yāyaṁ usmā sā tattheva vūpasameyya, kapallāni avasisseyyuṁ.
segs.e: Its heat would dissipate right there, and the shards would be left behind.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmīti pajānāti, jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmīti pajānāti.
segs.e: In the same way, feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissanti, sarīrāni avasissantīti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life has come to an end, everything that’s felt, since I no longer take pleasure in it, will become cool right here. Only bodily remains will be left.’
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu kho khīṇāsavo bhikkhu puññābhisaṅkhāraṁ vā abhisaṅkhareyya apuññābhisaṅkhāraṁ vā abhisaṅkhareyya āneñjābhisaṅkhāraṁ vā abhisaṅkhareyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would a mendicant who has ended the defilements still make good choices, bad choices, or imperturbable choices?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana saṅkhāresu asati, saṅkhāranirodhā api nu kho viññāṇaṁ paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there are no choices at all, with the cessation of choices, would consciousness still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana viññāṇe asati, viññāṇanirodhā api nu kho nāmarūpaṁ paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there’s no consciousness at all, would name and form still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana nāmarūpe asati, nāmarūpanirodhā api nu kho saḷāyatanaṁ paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there are no name and form at all, would the six sense fields still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana saḷāyatane asati, saḷāyatananirodhā api nu kho phasso paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there are no six sense fields at all, would contact still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana phasse asati, phassanirodhā api nu kho vedanā paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there’s no contact at all, would feeling still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana vedanāya asati, vedanānirodhā api nu kho taṇhā paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there’s no feeling at all, would craving still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana taṇhāya asati, taṇhānirodhā api nu kho upādānaṁ paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there’s no craving at all, would grasping still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana upādāne asati, upādānanirodhā api nu kho bhavo paññāyethā”ti.
segs.e: “And when there’s no grasping at all, would continued existence still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana bhave asati, bhavanirodhā api nu kho jāti paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there’s no continued existence at all, would rebirth still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sabbaso vā pana jātiyā asati, jātinirodhā api nu kho jarāmaraṇaṁ paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “And when there’s no rebirth at all, would old age and death still be found?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave, evametaṁ, bhikkhave, netaṁ aññathā.
segs.e: “Good, good, mendicants! That’s how it is, not otherwise.

segs.p: Saddahatha me taṁ, bhikkhave, adhimuccatha, nikkaṅkhā ettha hotha nibbicikicchā.
segs.e: Trust me on this, mendicants; be convinced. Have no doubts or uncertainties in this matter.
Just this is the end of suffering.”
Linked Discourses 12.52
6. Suffering
Grasping
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Upādāniyesu, bhikkhave, dhammesu assādānupassino viharato taṇhā pavaḍḍhati.
segs.e: “There are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.
Craving is a requirement for grasping.
Grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dasannaṁ vā kaṭṭhavāhānaṁ vīsāya vā kaṭṭhavāhānaṁ tiṁsāya vā kaṭṭhavāhānaṁ cattārīsāya vā kaṭṭhavāhānaṁ mahāaggikkhandho jaleyya.
segs.e: Suppose a great mass of fire was burning with ten, twenty, thirty, or forty loads of wood.

segs.p: Tatra puriso kālena kālaṁ sukkhāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya.
segs.e: And from time to time someone would toss in dry grass, cow dung, or wood.

segs.p: Evañhi so, bhikkhave, mahāaggikkhandho tadāhāro tadupādāno ciraṁ dīghamaddhānaṁ jaleyya.
segs.e: Fed and fuelled by that, the great mass of fire would burn for a long time.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, upādāniyesu dhammesu assādānupassino viharato taṇhā pavaḍḍhati.
segs.e: In the same way, there are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the gratification provided by these things, your craving grows.
Craving is a requirement for grasping. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Upādāniyesu, bhikkhave, dhammesu ādīnavānupassino viharato taṇhā nirujjhati.
segs.e: There are things that fuel grasping. When you concentrate on the drawbacks of these things, your craving ceases.
When craving ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases.
When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases.
When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

segs.p: “assutavā, bhikkhave, puthujjano imasmiṁ cātumahābhūtikasmiṁ kāyasmiṁ nibbindeyyapi virajjeyyapi vimucceyyapi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an unlearned ordinary person might become disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed from this body made up of the four principal states.
Why is that?

segs.p: Dissati, bhikkhave, imassa cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa ācayopi apacayopi ādānampi nikkhepanampi.
segs.e: This body made up of the four principal states is seen to accumulate and disperse, to be taken up and laid to rest.

segs.p: Tasmā tatrāssutavā puthujjano nibbindeyyapi virajjeyyapi vimucceyyapi.
segs.e: That’s why an unlearned ordinary person might become disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed from it.

segs.p: Yañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vuccati cittaṁ itipi, mano itipi, viññāṇaṁ itipi, tatrāssutavā puthujjano nālaṁ nibbindituṁ nālaṁ virajjituṁ nālaṁ vimuccituṁ.
segs.e: But an unlearned ordinary person is unable to become disillusioned, dispassionate, or freed from that which is called ‘mind’ and also ‘sentience’ and also ‘consciousness’.
Why is that?

segs.p: Dīgharattañhetaṁ, bhikkhave, assutavato puthujjanassa ajjhositaṁ mamāyitaṁ parāmaṭṭhaṁ:
segs.e: Because for a long time they’ve been attached to it, thought of it as their own, and mistaken it:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

segs.p: Tasmā tatrāssutavā puthujjano nālaṁ nibbindituṁ nālaṁ virajjituṁ nālaṁ vimuccituṁ.
segs.e: That’s why an unlearned ordinary person is unable to become disillusioned, dispassionate, or freed from it.

segs.p: Varaṁ, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano imaṁ cātumahābhūtikaṁ kāyaṁ attato upagaccheyya, na tveva cittaṁ.
segs.e: But an unlearned ordinary person would be better off taking this body made up of the four principal states to be their self, rather than the mind.
Why is that?

segs.p: Dissatāyaṁ, bhikkhave, cātumahābhūtiko kāyo ekampi vassaṁ tiṭṭhamāno dvepi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno tīṇipi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno cattāripi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno pañcapi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno dasapi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno vīsatipi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno tiṁsampi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno cattārīsampi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno paññāsampi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno vassasatampi tiṭṭhamāno, bhiyyopi tiṭṭhamāno.
segs.e: This body made up of the four principal states is seen to last for a year, or for two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or a hundred years, or even longer.

segs.p: Yañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vuccati cittaṁ itipi, mano itipi, viññāṇaṁ itipi, taṁ rattiyā ca divasassa ca aññadeva uppajjati aññaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: But that which is called ‘mind’ and also ‘sentience’ and also ‘consciousness’ arises as one thing and ceases as another all day and all night.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, makkaṭo araññe pavane caramāno sākhaṁ gaṇhati, taṁ muñcitvā aññaṁ gaṇhati, taṁ muñcitvā aññaṁ gaṇhati;
segs.e: It’s like a monkey moving through the forest. It grabs hold of one branch, lets it go, and grabs another; then it lets that go and grabs yet another.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, yamidaṁ vuccati cittaṁ itipi, mano itipi, viññāṇaṁ itipi, taṁ rattiyā ca divasassa ca aññadeva uppajjati aññaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: In the same way, that which is called ‘mind’ and also ‘sentience’ and also ‘consciousness’ arises as one thing and ceases as another all day and all night.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaṁyeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti:
segs.e: In this case, a learned noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

segs.p: ‘iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
segs.e: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati—
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:
Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease.
When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati;
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: nibbindaṁ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati, vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

7. The Great Chapter
Unlearned (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Assutavā, bhikkhave, puthujjano imasmiṁ cātumahābhūtikasmiṁ kāyasmiṁ nibbindeyyapi virajjeyyapi vimucceyyapi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an unlearned ordinary person might become disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed from this body made up of the four principal states.
Why is that?

segs.p: Dissati, bhikkhave, imassa cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa ācayopi apacayopi ādānampi nikkhepanampi.

Why is that?

segs.p: Dissatāyaṁ, bhikkhave, cātumahābhūtiko kāyo ekampi vassaṁ tiṭṭhamāno dvepi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno tīṇipi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno cattāripi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno pañcapi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno dasapi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno vīsatipi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno tiṁsampi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno cattārīsampi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno paññāsampi vassāni tiṭṭhamāno vassasatampi tiṭṭhamāno, bhiyyopi tiṭṭhamāno.
segs.e: This body made up of the four principal states is seen to last for a year, or for two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or a hundred years, or even longer.

segs.p: Yañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vuccati cittaṁ itipi, mano itipi, viññāṇaṁ itipi, taṁ rattiyā ca divasassa ca aññadeva uppajjati aññaṁ nirujjhati.
segs.e: But that which is called ‘mind’ and also ‘sentience’ and also ‘consciousness’ arises as one thing and ceases as another all day and all night.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaṁyeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti:
segs.e: In this case, a learned noble disciple carefully and rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

segs.p: ‘iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
segs.e: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhatī’ti.
segs.e: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases.’

segs.p: Sukhavedaniyaṁ, bhikkhave, phassaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhavedanā.
segs.e: Pleasant feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

segs.p: Tasseva sukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṁ tajjaṁ vedayitaṁ sukhavedaniyaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppannā sukhavedanā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati.
segs.e: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as pleasant, the corresponding pleasant feeling ceases and stops.

segs.p: Dukkhavedaniyaṁ, bhikkhave, phassaṁ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhavedanā.
segs.e: Painful feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful.

segs.p: Tasseva dukkhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṁ tajjaṁ vedayitaṁ dukkhavedaniyaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppannā dukkhavedanā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati.
segs.e: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as painful, the corresponding painful feeling ceases and stops.

segs.p: Adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṁ, bhikkhave, phassaṁ paṭicca uppajjati adukkhamasukhavedanā.
segs.e: Neutral feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as neutral.

segs.p: Tasseva adukkhamasukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṁ tajjaṁ vedayitaṁ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppannā adukkhamasukhavedanā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati.
segs.e: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as neutral, the corresponding neutral feeling ceases and stops.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ kaṭṭhānaṁ saṅghaṭṭanasamodhānā usmā jāyati tejo abhinibbattati. Tesaṁyeva dvinnaṁ kaṭṭhānaṁ nānākatavinibbhogā yā tajjā usmā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati;
segs.e: When you rub two sticks together, heat is generated and fire is produced. But when you part the sticks and lay them aside, any corresponding heat ceases and stops.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, sukhavedaniyaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppajjati sukhavedanā.
segs.e: In the same way, pleasant feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant.

segs.p: Tasseva sukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṁ tajjaṁ vedayitaṁ sukhavedaniyaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppannā sukhavedanā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati …pe…
segs.e: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as pleasant, the corresponding pleasant feeling ceases and stops.
Painful feeling …
Neutral feeling arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as neutral.

segs.p: Tasseva adukkhamasukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṁ tajjaṁ vedayitaṁ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṁ phassaṁ paṭicca uppannā adukkhamasukhavedanā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati.
segs.e: With the cessation of that contact to be experienced as neutral, the corresponding neutral feeling ceases and stops.

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako phassepi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati;
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with contact, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: nibbindaṁ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati, vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

7. The Great Chapter
A Child’s Flesh
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four fuels maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.
What four?

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṁ catutthaṁ.
segs.e: Edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: These are the four fuels that maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.
And how should you regard edible food?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dve jāyampatikā parittaṁ sambalaṁ ādāya kantāramaggaṁ paṭipajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: Suppose a couple who were husband and wife set out to cross a desert, taking limited supplies.
They had an only child, dear and beloved.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ jāyampatikānaṁ kantāragatānaṁ yā parittā sambalamattā, sā parikkhayaṁ pariyādānaṁ gaccheyya.
segs.e: As the couple were crossing the desert their limited quantity of supplies would run out,
and they’d still have the rest of the desert to cross.

segs.p: Atha kho tesaṁ, bhikkhave, dvinnaṁ jāyampatikānaṁ evamassa:
segs.e: Then it would occur to that couple:

segs.p: ‘amhākaṁ kho yā parittā sambalamattā sā parikkhīṇā pariyādiṇṇā.
segs.e: ‘Our limited quantity of supplies has run out,
and we still have the rest of the desert to cross.

segs.p: Yannūna mayaṁ imaṁ ekaputtakaṁ piyaṁ manāpaṁ vadhitvā vallūrañca soṇḍikañca karitvā puttamaṁsāni khādantā evaṁ taṁ kantārāvasesaṁ nitthareyyāma, mā sabbeva tayo vinassimhā’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t we kill our only child, so dear and beloved, and prepare dried and spiced meat? Then we can make it across the desert by eating our child’s flesh. Let not all three perish.’

segs.p: Atha kho te, bhikkhave, dve jāyampatikā taṁ ekaputtakaṁ piyaṁ manāpaṁ vadhitvā vallūrañca soṇḍikañca karitvā puttamaṁsāni khādantā evaṁ taṁ kantārāvasesaṁ nitthareyyuṁ.
segs.e: Then that couple would kill their only child, so dear and beloved, and prepare dried and spiced meat. They’d make it across the desert by eating their child’s flesh.

segs.p: Te puttamaṁsāni ceva khādeyyuṁ, ure ca paṭipiseyyuṁ:
segs.e: And as they’d eat their child’s flesh, they’d beat their breasts and cry:
‘Where are you, our only child? Where are you, our only child?’
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu te davāya vā āhāraṁ āhāreyyuṁ, madāya vā āhāraṁ āhāreyyuṁ, maṇḍanāya vā āhāraṁ āhāreyyuṁ, vibhūsanāya vā āhāraṁ āhāreyyun”ti?
segs.e: Would they eat that food for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Nanu te, bhikkhave, yāvadeva kantārassa nittharaṇatthāya āhāraṁ āhāreyyun”ti?
segs.e: “Wouldn’t they eat that food just so they could make it across the desert?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “‘Evameva khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, kabaḷīkāro āhāro daṭṭhabbo’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: “I say that this is how you should regard edible food.

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāre, bhikkhave, āhāre pariññāte pañca kāmaguṇiko rāgo pariññāto hoti.
segs.e: When edible food is completely understood, desire for the five kinds of sensual stimulation is completely understood.

segs.p: Pañca kāmaguṇike rāge pariññāte natthi taṁ saṁyojanaṁ yena saṁyojanena saṁyutto ariyasāvako puna imaṁ lokaṁ āgaccheyya.
segs.e: When desire for the five kinds of sensual stimulation is completely understood, a noble disciple is bound by no fetter that might return them again to this world.
And how should you regard contact as fuel?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gāvī niccammā kuṭṭañce nissāya tiṭṭheyya. Ye kuṭṭanissitā pāṇā te naṁ khādeyyuṁ.
segs.e: Suppose there was a flayed cow. If she stands by a wall, the creatures on the wall bite her.

segs.p: Rukkhañce nissāya tiṭṭheyya, ye rukkhanissitā pāṇā te naṁ khādeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If she stands under a tree, the creatures in the tree bite her.

segs.p: Udakañce nissāya tiṭṭheyya, ye udakanissitā pāṇā te naṁ khādeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If she stands in some water, the creatures in the water bite her.

segs.p: Ākāsañce nissāya tiṭṭheyya, ye ākāsanissitā pāṇā te naṁ khādeyyuṁ.
segs.e: If she stands in the open, the creatures in the open bite her.

segs.p: Yaṁ yadeva hi sā, bhikkhave, gāvī niccammā nissāya tiṭṭheyya, ye tannissitā pāṇā te naṁ khādeyyuṁ.
segs.e: Wherever that flayed cow stands, the creatures there would bite her.
I say that this is how you should regard contact as fuel.

segs.p: Phasse, bhikkhave, āhāre pariññāte tisso vedanā pariññātā honti.
segs.e: When contact as fuel is completely understood, the three feelings are completely understood.

segs.p: Tīsu vedanāsu pariññātāsu ariyasāvakassa natthi kiñci uttarikaraṇīyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When the three feelings are completely understood, a noble disciple has nothing further to do, I say.
And how should you regard mental intention as fuel?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, aṅgārakāsu sādhikaporisā puṇṇā aṅgārānaṁ vītaccikānaṁ vītadhūmānaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose there was a pit of glowing coals deeper than a man’s height, filled with glowing coals that neither flamed nor smoked.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhappaṭikūlo.
segs.e: Then a person would come along who wants to live and doesn’t want to die, who wants to be happy and recoils from pain.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ dve balavanto purisā nānābāhāsu gahetvā taṁ aṅgārakāsuṁ upakaḍḍheyyuṁ.
segs.e: Two strong men would grab them by the arms and drag them toward the pit of glowing coals.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, tassa purisassa ārakāvassa cetanā ārakā patthanā ārakā paṇidhi.
segs.e: Then that person’s intention, aim, and wish would be to get far away.
Why is that?
Because that person would think:

segs.p: ‘imañcāhaṁ aṅgārakāsuṁ papatissāmi, tatonidānaṁ maraṇaṁ vā nigacchāmi maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘If I fall in that pit of glowing coals, that will result in my death or deadly pain.’
I say that this is how you should regard mental intention as fuel.

segs.p: Manosañcetanāya, bhikkhave, āhāre pariññāte tisso taṇhā pariññātā honti.
segs.e: When mental intention as fuel is completely understood, the three cravings are completely understood.

segs.p: Tīsu taṇhāsu pariññātāsu ariyasāvakassa natthi kiñci uttarikaraṇīyanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When the three cravings are completely understood, a noble disciple has nothing further to do, I say.
And how should you regard consciousness as fuel?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, coraṁ āgucāriṁ gahetvā rañño dasseyyuṁ:
segs.e: Suppose they were to arrest a bandit, a criminal and present him to the king, saying:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ te, deva, coro āgucārī, imassa yaṁ icchasi taṁ daṇḍaṁ paṇehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Your Majesty, this is a bandit, a criminal. Punish him as you will.’
The king would say:

segs.p: ‘gacchatha, bho, imaṁ purisaṁ pubbaṇhasamayaṁ sattisatena hanathā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Go, my men, and strike this man in the morning with a hundred spears!’
The king’s men did as they were told.
Then at midday the king would say:
‘Look here, how is that man?’
‘He’s still alive, Your Majesty.’
The king would say:

segs.p: ‘gacchatha, bho, taṁ purisaṁ majjhanhikasamayaṁ sattisatena hanathā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Go, my men, and strike this man in the middle of the day with a hundred spears!’
The king’s men did as they were told.
Then late in the afternoon the king would say:
‘Look here, how is that man?’
‘He’s still alive, Your Majesty.’
The king would say:

segs.p: ‘gacchatha, bho, taṁ purisaṁ sāyanhasamayaṁ sattisatena hanathā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Go, my men, and strike this man in the late afternoon with a hundred spears!’
The king’s men did as they were told.
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu so puriso divasaṁ tīhi sattisatehi haññamāno tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvediyethā”ti?
segs.e: Would that man experience pain and distress from being struck with three hundred spears a day?”

segs.p: “Ekissāpi, bhante, sattiyā haññamāno tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvediyetha;
segs.e: “Sir, that man would experience pain and distress from being struck with one spear,

segs.p: ko pana vādo tīhi sattisatehi haññamāno”ti.
segs.e: let alone three hundred spears!”
“I say that this is how you should regard consciousness as fuel.

segs.p: Viññāṇe, bhikkhave, āhāre pariññāte nāmarūpaṁ pariññātaṁ hoti, nāmarūpe pariññāte ariyasāvakassa natthi kiñci uttarikaraṇīyanti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: When consciousness as fuel is completely understood, name and form are completely understood. When name and form are completely understood, a noble disciple has nothing further to do, I say.”

7. The Great Chapter
If There is Desire
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four fuels maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.
What four?

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṁ catutthaṁ.
segs.e: Edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āhārā bhūtānaṁ vā sattānaṁ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṁ vā anuggahāya.
segs.e: These are the four fuels that maintain sentient beings that have been born and help those about to be born.

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāre ce, bhikkhave, āhāre atthi rāgo atthi nandī atthi taṇhā, patiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: If there is desire, relishing, and craving for edible food, consciousness becomes established there and grows.

segs.p: Yattha patiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ, atthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.

segs.p: Yattha atthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, atthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are conceived, there is the growth of choices.

segs.p: Yattha atthi saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi, atthi tattha āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti.
segs.e: Where choices grow, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, atthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ, sasokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, sadaraṁ saupāyāsanti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say this is full of sorrow, anguish, and distress.
If there is desire, relishing, and craving for contact as fuel …
If there is desire, relishing, and craving for mental intention as fuel …

segs.p: viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre atthi rāgo atthi nandī atthi taṇhā, patiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: If there is desire, relishing, and craving for consciousness as fuel, consciousness becomes established there and grows.

segs.p: Yattha patiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ, atthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.

segs.p: Yattha atthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, atthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are conceived, there is the growth of choices.

segs.e: Where choices grow, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, atthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ, sasokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, sadaraṁ saupāyāsanti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say this is full of sorrow, anguish, and distress.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rajako vā cittakārako vā sati rajanāya vā lākhāya vā haliddiyā vā nīliyā vā mañjiṭṭhāya vā suparimaṭṭhe vā phalake bhittiyā vā dussapaṭṭe vā itthirūpaṁ vā purisarūpaṁ vā abhinimmineyya sabbaṅgapaccaṅgaṁ;
segs.e: Suppose an artist or painter had some dye, red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder. And on a polished plank or a wall or a canvas they’d create the form of a woman or a man, whole in its major and minor limbs.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, kabaḷīkāre ce āhāre atthi rāgo atthi nandī atthi taṇhā, patiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, if there is desire, relishing, and craving for edible food, consciousness becomes established there and grows.

segs.p: Yattha patiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ, atthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.

segs.p: Yattha atthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, atthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are conceived, there is the growth of choices.

segs.p: Yattha atthi saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi, atthi tattha āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti.
