segs.e: Where choices grow, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, atthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ, sasokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, sadaraṁ saupāyāsanti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say this is full of sorrow, anguish, and distress.
If there is desire, relishing, and craving for contact as fuel …
If there is desire, relishing, and craving for mental intention as fuel …

segs.p: viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre atthi rāgo atthi nandī atthi taṇhā, patiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: If there is desire, relishing, and craving for consciousness as fuel, consciousness becomes established there and grows.

segs.p: Yattha patiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ virūḷhaṁ, atthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is established and grows, name and form are conceived.

segs.p: Yattha atthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, atthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are conceived, there is the growth of choices.

segs.p: Yattha atthi saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi, atthi tattha āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti.
segs.e: Where choices grow, there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, atthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha atthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ, sasokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, sadaraṁ saupāyāsanti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where there is rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say this is full of sorrow, anguish, and distress.

segs.p: Kabaḷīkāre ce, bhikkhave, āhāre natthi rāgo natthi nandī natthi taṇhā, appatiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ avirūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for edible food, consciousness does not become established there and doesn’t grow.

segs.p: Yattha appatiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ avirūḷhaṁ, natthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, name and form are not conceived.

segs.p: Yattha natthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, natthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are not conceived, there is no growth of choices.

segs.p: Yattha natthi saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi, natthi tattha āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti.
segs.e: Where choices don’t grow, there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, natthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ, asokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, adaraṁ anupāyāsanti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say there’s no sorrow, anguish, and distress.
If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for contact as fuel …
If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for mental intention as fuel …

segs.p: viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre natthi rāgo natthi nandī natthi taṇhā, appatiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ avirūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for consciousness as fuel, consciousness doesn’t become established there and doesn’t grow.

segs.p: Yattha appatiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ avirūḷhaṁ, natthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, name and form are not conceived.

segs.p: Yattha natthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, natthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are not conceived, there is no growth of choices.

segs.p: Yattha natthi saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi, natthi tattha āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti.
segs.e: Where choices don’t grow, there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, natthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ, asokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, adaraṁ anupāyāsanti vadāmi.
segs.e: Where there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say there’s no sorrow, anguish, and distress.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgāraṁ vā kūṭāgārasālaṁ vā uttarāya vā dakkhiṇāya vā pācīnāya vā vātapānā sūriye uggacchante vātapānena rasmi pavisitvā kvāssa patiṭṭhitā”ti?
segs.e: Suppose there was a bungalow or a hall with a peaked roof, with windows on the northern, southern, or eastern side. When the sun rises and a ray of light enters through a window, where would it land?”
“On the western wall, sir.”

segs.p: “Pacchimā ce, bhikkhave, bhitti nāssa kvāssa patiṭṭhitā”ti?
segs.e: “If there was no western wall, where would it land?”
“On the ground, sir.”
“If there was no ground, where would it land?”
“In water, sir.”
“If there was no water, where would it land?”
“It wouldn’t land, sir.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, kabaḷīkāre ce āhāre natthi rāgo natthi nandī natthi taṇhā …pe….
segs.e: “In the same way, if there is no desire, relishing, and craving for edible food, consciousness does not become established there and doesn’t grow. …
If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for contact as fuel …
If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for mental intention as fuel …

segs.p: viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre natthi rāgo natthi nandī natthi taṇhā, appatiṭṭhitaṁ tattha viññāṇaṁ avirūḷhaṁ.
segs.e: If there is no desire, relishing, and craving for consciousness as fuel, consciousness doesn’t become established there and doesn’t grow.

segs.p: Yattha appatiṭṭhitaṁ viññāṇaṁ avirūḷhaṁ, natthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti.
segs.e: Where consciousness is not established and doesn’t grow, name and form are not conceived.

segs.p: Yattha natthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, natthi tattha saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi.
segs.e: Where name and form are not conceived, there is no growth of choices.

segs.p: Yattha natthi saṅkhārānaṁ vuddhi, natthi tattha āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti.
segs.e: Where choices don’t grow, there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti, natthi tattha āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: Where there is no regeneration into a new state of existence in the future, there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future.

segs.p: Yattha natthi āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇaṁ asokaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, adaraṁ anupāyāsanti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: Where there is no rebirth, old age, and death in the future, I say there’s no sorrow, anguish, and distress.”
Linked Discourses 12.65
7. The Great Chapter
The City
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Pubbe me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, before my awakening—when I was still unawakened but intent on awakening—I thought:

segs.p: ‘kicchā vatāyaṁ loko āpanno jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca.
segs.e: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble. It’s born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn,

segs.p: Atha ca panimassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṁ nappajānāti jarāmaraṇassa.
segs.e: yet it doesn’t understand how to escape from this suffering, from old age and death.

segs.p: Kudāssu nāma imassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṁ paññāyissati jarāmaraṇassā’ti?
segs.e: Oh, when will an escape be found from this suffering, from old age and death?’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā jarāmaraṇan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there old age and death? What is a requirement for old age and death?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When rebirth exists there’s old age and death. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.’
Then it occurred to me:
‘When what exists is there rebirth? …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
What is a requirement for name and form?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘viññāṇe kho sati nāmarūpaṁ hoti, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When consciousness exists there are name and form. Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho sati viññāṇaṁ hoti, kiṁpaccayā viññāṇan’ti?
segs.e: ‘When what exists is there consciousness? What is a requirement for consciousness?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:

segs.p: ‘nāmarūpe kho sati viññāṇaṁ hoti, nāmarūpapaccayā viññāṇan’ti.
segs.e: ‘When name and form exist there’s consciousness. Name and form are requirements for consciousness.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: paccudāvattati kho idaṁ viññāṇaṁ nāmarūpamhā na paraṁ gacchati.
segs.e: This consciousness turns back from name and form, and doesn’t go beyond that.

segs.p: Ettāvatā jāyetha vā jīyetha vā mīyetha vā cavetha vā upapajjetha vā, yadidaṁ nāmarūpapaccayā viññāṇaṁ;
segs.e: This is the extent to which one may be reborn, grow old, die, pass away, or reappear. That is: name and form are requirements for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: ‘Samudayo, samudayo’ti kho me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṁ udapādi ñāṇaṁ udapādi paññā udapādi vijjā udapādi āloko udapādi.
segs.e: ‘Origination, origination.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in me regarding teachings not learned before from another.
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati, jarāmaraṇaṁ na hoti;
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no old age and death?
When what ceases do old age and death cease?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:
‘When rebirth doesn’t exist there is no old age and death.
When rebirth ceases old age and death cease.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati jāti na hoti …pe…
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no rebirth …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
six sense fields …
name and form?
When what ceases do name and form cease?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:
‘When consciousness doesn’t exist there is no name and form.
When consciousness ceases name and form cease.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘kimhi nu kho asati viññāṇaṁ na hoti;
segs.e: ‘When what doesn’t exist is there no consciousness?
When what ceases does consciousness cease?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo:
segs.e: Then, through rational application of mind, I penetrated with wisdom:
‘When name and form don’t exist, there is no consciousness.
When name and form cease, consciousness ceases.’
Then it occurred to me:

segs.p: adhigato kho myāyaṁ maggo bodhāya yadidaṁ—
segs.e: I have discovered the path to awakening. That is:
When name and form cease, consciousness ceases.
When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.
When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

segs.p: ‘Nirodho, nirodho’ti kho me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṁ udapādi ñāṇaṁ udapādi paññā udapādi vijjā udapādi āloko udapādi.
segs.e: ‘Cessation, cessation.’ Such was the vision, knowledge, wisdom, realization, and light that arose in me regarding teachings not learned before from another.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso araññe pavane caramāno passeyya purāṇaṁ maggaṁ purāṇañjasaṁ pubbakehi manussehi anuyātaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose a person was walking through a forest. They’d see an ancient path, an ancient route traveled by humans in the past.
Following it along,

segs.p: Tamanugacchanto passeyya purāṇaṁ nagaraṁ purāṇaṁ rājadhāniṁ pubbakehi manussehi ajjhāvuṭṭhaṁ ārāmasampannaṁ vanasampannaṁ pokkharaṇīsampannaṁ uddhāpavantaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: they’d see an ancient city, an ancient capital, inhabited by humans in the past. It was lovely, complete with parks, groves, lotus ponds, and embankments.

segs.p: Atha kho so, bhikkhave, puriso rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā āroceyya:
segs.e: Then that person would inform a king or their chief minister:

segs.p: ‘yagghe, bhante, jāneyyāsi—ahaṁ addasaṁ araññe pavane caramāno purāṇaṁ maggaṁ purāṇañjasaṁ pubbakehi manussehi anuyātaṁ tamanugacchiṁ.
segs.e: ‘Please sir, you should know this. While walking through a forest I saw an ancient path, an ancient route traveled by humans in the past.

segs.p: Tamanugacchanto addasaṁ purāṇaṁ nagaraṁ purāṇaṁ rājadhāniṁ pubbakehi manussehi ajjhāvuṭṭhaṁ ārāmasampannaṁ vanasampannaṁ pokkharaṇīsampannaṁ uddhāpavantaṁ ramaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: Following it along I saw an ancient city, an ancient capital, inhabited by humans in the past. It was lovely, complete with parks, groves, lotus ponds, and embankments.
Sir, you should rebuild that city!’

segs.p: Atha kho so, bhikkhave, rājā vā rājamahāmatto vā taṁ nagaraṁ māpeyya.
segs.e: Then that king or their chief minister would have that city rebuilt.

segs.p: Tadassa nagaraṁ aparena samayena iddhañceva phītañca bāhujaññaṁ ākiṇṇamanussaṁ vuddhivepullappattaṁ.
segs.e: And after some time that city was successful and prosperous, populous and full of people, attained to growth and expansion.

segs.p: Evameva khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, addasaṁ purāṇaṁ maggaṁ purāṇañjasaṁ pubbakehi sammāsambuddhehi anuyātaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, I saw an ancient path, an ancient route traveled by fully awakened Buddhas in the past.

segs.p: Katamo ca so, bhikkhave, purāṇamaggo purāṇañjaso pubbakehi sammāsambuddhehi anuyāto?
segs.e: And what is that ancient path, the ancient route traveled by fully awakened Buddhas in the past?
It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho so, bhikkhave, purāṇamaggo purāṇañjaso pubbakehi sammāsambuddhehi anuyāto, tamanugacchiṁ;
segs.e: This is that ancient path, the ancient route traveled by fully awakened Buddhas in the past.
Following it along, I directly knew old age and death,
their origin,
their cessation,
and the practice that leads to their cessation.
Following it along, I directly knew rebirth …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
consciousness …
Following it along, I directly knew choices,
their origin,
their cessation,
and the practice that leads to their cessation.

segs.p: Tadabhiññāya ācikkhiṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ upāsakānaṁ upāsikānaṁ.
segs.e: Having directly known this, I told the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

segs.p: Tayidaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṁ bāhujaññaṁ puthubhūtaṁ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitan”ti.
segs.e: And that’s how this spiritual life has become successful and prosperous, extensive, popular, widespread, and fully revealed among gods and humans.”
Linked Discourses 12.66
7. The Great Chapter
Probing Within
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṁ nāma kurūnaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kurus, near the Kuru town named Kammāsadamma.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, do you probe within?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,
“Sir, I probe within.”

segs.p: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, sammasasi antaraṁ sammasan”ti?
segs.e: “But mendicant, how do you probe within?”
Then that mendicant answered,

segs.p: Yathā so bhikkhu byākāsi na so bhikkhu bhagavato cittaṁ ārādhesi.
segs.e: but the Buddha was not happy with the answer.

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,
“Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One!

segs.p: yaṁ bhagavā antaraṁ sammasaṁ bhāseyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: Let the Buddha speak of probing within. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”
“Well then, Ānanda, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammasamāno sammasati antaraṁ sammasaṁ:
segs.e: “Take a mendicant who probes within:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho idaṁ anekavidhaṁ nānappakārakaṁ dukkhaṁ loke uppajjati jarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: ‘The suffering that arises in the world starting with old age and death takes many and diverse forms.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho dukkhaṁ kiṁnidānaṁ kiṁsamudayaṁ kiṁjātikaṁ kiṁpabhavaṁ, kismiṁ sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, kismiṁ asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hotī’ti?
segs.e: But what is the source of this suffering? When what exists do old age and death come to be? And when what does not exist do old age and death not come to be?’
While probing they know:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho idaṁ anekavidhaṁ nānappakārakaṁ dukkhaṁ loke uppajjati jarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: ‘The suffering that arises in the world starting with old age and death takes many and diverse forms.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho dukkhaṁ upadhinidānaṁ upadhisamudayaṁ upadhijātikaṁ upadhipabhavaṁ, upadhismiṁ sati jarāmaraṇaṁ hoti, upadhismiṁ asati jarāmaraṇaṁ na hotī’ti.
segs.e: The source of this suffering is attachment. When attachments exist old age and death come to be. And when attachments do not exist old age and death don’t come to be.’

segs.p: So jarāmaraṇañca pajānāti jarāmaraṇasamudayañca pajānāti jarāmaraṇanirodhañca pajānāti yā ca jarāmaraṇanirodhasāruppagāminī paṭipadā tañca pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand old age and death, their origin, their cessation, and the fitting practice for their cessation.
And they practice in line with that path.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya paṭipanno jarāmaraṇanirodhāya.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of old age and death.
They probe further within:

segs.p: ‘upadhi panāyaṁ kiṁnidāno kiṁsamudayo kiṁjātiko kiṁpabhavo, kismiṁ sati upadhi hoti, kismiṁ asati upadhi na hotī’ti?
segs.e: ‘But what is the source of this attachment? When what exists does attachment come to be? And when what does not exist does attachment not come to be?’
While probing they know:

segs.p: ‘upadhi taṇhānidāno taṇhāsamudayo taṇhājātiko taṇhāpabhavo, taṇhāya sati upadhi hoti, taṇhāya asati upadhi na hotī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The source of this attachment is craving. When craving exists attachments come to be. And when craving doesn’t exist attachments don’t come to be.’

segs.p: So upadhiñca pajānāti upadhisamudayañca pajānāti upadhinirodhañca pajānāti yā ca upadhinirodhasāruppagāminī paṭipadā tañca pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand attachments, their origin, their cessation, and the fitting practice for their cessation.
And they practice in line with that path.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya paṭipanno upadhinirodhāya.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who is practicing for the complete ending of suffering, for the cessation of attachments.
They probe further within:

segs.p: ‘taṇhā panāyaṁ kattha uppajjamānā uppajjati, kattha nivisamānā nivisatī’ti?
segs.e: ‘But where does that craving arise and where does it settle?’
While probing they know:

segs.p: yaṁ kho loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.
segs.e: ‘That craving arises and settles on whatever in the world seems nice and pleasant.
And what in the world seems nice and pleasant?

segs.p: Cakkhuṁ loke piyarūpaṁ, sātarūpaṁ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati, ettha nivisamānā nivisati.
segs.e: The eye in the world seems nice and pleasant, and it is there that craving arises and settles.
The ear …
nose …
tongue …
body …

segs.p: mano loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ, etthesā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati ettha nivisamānā nivisati.
segs.e: mind in the world seems nice and pleasant, and it is there that craving arises and settles.’

segs.p: Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ niccato addakkhuṁ sukhato addakkhuṁ attato addakkhuṁ ārogyato addakkhuṁ khemato addakkhuṁ.
segs.e: There were ascetics and brahmins of the past who saw the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as permanent, as pleasurable, as self, as healthy, and as safe.
Their craving grew.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ vaḍḍhesuṁ te upadhiṁ vaḍḍhesuṁ.
segs.e: As their craving grew, their attachments grew.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ vaḍḍhesuṁ te dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhesuṁ.
segs.e: As their attachments grew, their suffering grew.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhesuṁ te na parimucciṁsu jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘na parimucciṁsu dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: And as their suffering grew, they were not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They were not freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ niccato dakkhissanti sukhato dakkhissanti attato dakkhissanti ārogyato dakkhissanti khemato dakkhissanti.
segs.e: There will be ascetics and brahmins in the future who will see the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as permanent, as pleasurable, as self, as healthy, and as safe.
Their craving will grow.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ vaḍḍhissanti te upadhiṁ vaḍḍhissanti.
segs.e: As their craving grows, their attachments will grow.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ vaḍḍhissanti te dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhissanti.
segs.e: As their attachments grow, their suffering will grow.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhissanti te na parimuccissanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘na parimuccissanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: And as their suffering grows, they will not be freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They will not be freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ niccato passanti sukhato passanti attato passanti ārogyato passanti khemato passanti.
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins in the present who see the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as permanent, as pleasurable, as self, as healthy, and as safe.
Their craving grows.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ vaḍḍhenti te upadhiṁ vaḍḍhenti.
segs.e: As their craving grows, their attachments grow.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ vaḍḍhenti te dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhenti.
segs.e: As their attachments grow, their suffering grows.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhenti te na parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘na parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: And as their suffering grows, they are not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They are not freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āpānīyakaṁso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bronze goblet of beverage that had a nice color, aroma, and flavor.
But it was mixed with poison.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito.
segs.e: Then along comes a man struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.
They’d say to him:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ te, ambho purisa, āpānīyakaṁso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno;
segs.e: ‘Here, my man, this bronze goblet of beverage has a nice color, aroma, and flavor.
But it’s mixed with poison.
Drink it if you like.

segs.p: Pivato hi kho taṁ chādessati vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi, pivitvā ca pana tatonidānaṁ maraṇaṁ vā nigacchasi maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhan’ti.
segs.e: If you drink it, the color, aroma, and flavor will be appetizing, but it will result in death or deadly pain.’

segs.p: So taṁ āpānīyakaṁsaṁ sahasā appaṭisaṅkhā piveyya, nappaṭinissajjeyya.
segs.e: He wouldn’t put that beverage down. Hastily, without reflection, he’d drink it,

segs.p: So tatonidānaṁ maraṇaṁ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: resulting in death or deadly pain.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci atītamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ …pe…
segs.e: In the same way, there are ascetics and brahmins of the past …
future …

segs.p: etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ niccato passanti sukhato passanti attato passanti ārogyato passanti khemato passanti, te taṇhaṁ vaḍḍhenti.
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins in the present who see the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as permanent, as pleasurable, as self, as healthy, and as safe. Their craving grows.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ vaḍḍhenti te upadhiṁ vaḍḍhenti.
segs.e: As their craving grows, their attachments grow.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ vaḍḍhenti te dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhenti.
segs.e: As their attachments grow, their suffering grows.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ vaḍḍhenti te na parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘na parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: And as their suffering grows, they are not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They are not freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ aniccato addakkhuṁ dukkhato addakkhuṁ anattato addakkhuṁ rogato addakkhuṁ bhayato addakkhuṁ,
segs.e: There were ascetics and brahmins of the past who saw the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self, as diseased, and as dangerous.
They gave up craving.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ pajahiṁsu te upadhiṁ pajahiṁsu.
segs.e: Giving up craving, they gave up attachments.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ pajahiṁsu te dukkhaṁ pajahiṁsu.
segs.e: Giving up attachments, they gave up suffering.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ pajahiṁsu te parimucciṁsu jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimucciṁsu dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Giving up suffering, they were freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They were freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ aniccato dakkhissanti dukkhato dakkhissanti anattato dakkhissanti rogato dakkhissanti bhayato dakkhissanti,
segs.e: There will be ascetics and brahmins in the future who will see the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self, as diseased, and as dangerous.
They will give up craving.
Giving up craving …
they will be freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Yepi hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ aniccato passanti dukkhato passanti anattato passanti rogato passanti bhayato passanti,
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins in the present who see the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self, as diseased, and as dangerous.
They give up craving.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ pajahanti te upadhiṁ pajahanti.
segs.e: Giving up craving, they give up attachments.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ pajahanti te dukkhaṁ pajahanti.
segs.e: Giving up attachments, they give up suffering.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ pajahanti te parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Giving up suffering, they are freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They are freed from suffering, I say.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āpānīyakaṁso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bronze goblet of beverage that had a nice color, aroma, and flavor.
But it was mixed with poison.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito.
segs.e: Then along comes a man struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.
They’d say to him:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ te, ambho purisa, āpānīyakaṁso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno
segs.e: ‘Here, my man, this bronze goblet of beverage has a nice color, aroma, and flavor.
But it’s mixed with poison.
Drink it if you like.

segs.p: Pivato hi kho taṁ chādessati vaṇṇenapi gandhenapi rasenapi; pivitvā ca pana tatonidānaṁ maraṇaṁ vā nigacchasi maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhan’ti.
segs.e: If you drink it, its nice color, aroma, and flavor will refresh you. But drinking it will result in death or deadly pain.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, tassa purisassa evamassa:
segs.e: Then that man might think:

segs.p: ‘sakkā kho me ayaṁ surāpipāsitā pānīyena vā vinetuṁ dadhimaṇḍakena vā vinetuṁ bhaṭṭhaloṇikāya vā vinetuṁ loṇasovīrakena vā vinetuṁ, na tvevāhaṁ taṁ piveyyaṁ, yaṁ mama assa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘I can allay my thirst with a fermented drink of beer, buttermilk, salt lassi, or salted infusion. But in any case, I shouldn’t drink that beverage, for it would be for my lasting harm and suffering.’

segs.p: So taṁ āpānīyakaṁsaṁ paṭisaṅkhā na piveyya, paṭinissajjeyya.
segs.e: He’d put that beverage down. After appraisal, he wouldn’t drink it,

segs.p: So tatonidānaṁ na maraṇaṁ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhaṁ.
segs.e: and it wouldn’t result in death or deadly pain.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci atītamaddhānaṁ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ aniccato addakkhuṁ dukkhato addakkhuṁ anattato addakkhuṁ rogato addakkhuṁ bhayato addakkhuṁ,
segs.e: In the same way, there were ascetics and brahmins of the past who saw the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self, as diseased, and as dangerous.
They gave up craving.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ pajahiṁsu te upadhiṁ pajahiṁsu.
segs.e: Giving up craving, they gave up attachments.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ pajahiṁsu te dukkhaṁ pajahiṁsu.
segs.e: Giving up attachments, they gave up suffering.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ pajahiṁsu te parimucciṁsu jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimucciṁsu dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: Giving up suffering, they were freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They were freed from suffering, I say.
There will be ascetics and brahmins in the future …

segs.p: etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yaṁ loke piyarūpaṁ sātarūpaṁ taṁ aniccato passanti dukkhato passanti anattato passanti rogato passanti bhayato passanti,
segs.e: There are ascetics and brahmins in the present who see the things that seem nice and pleasant in the world as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self, as diseased, and as dangerous.
They give up craving.

segs.p: Ye taṇhaṁ pajahanti te upadhiṁ pajahanti.
segs.e: Giving up craving, they give up attachments.

segs.p: Ye upadhiṁ pajahanti te dukkhaṁ pajahanti.
segs.e: Giving up attachments, they give up suffering.

segs.p: Ye dukkhaṁ pajahanti te parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, ‘parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: Giving up suffering, they are freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They are freed from suffering, I say.”
Linked Discourses 12.67
7. The Great Chapter
Sheaves of Reeds

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita came out of retreat, went to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, sayaṅkataṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, paraṅkataṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca jarāmaraṇaṁ, udāhu asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ jarāmaraṇan”ti?
segs.e: “Well, Reverend Sāriputta, are old age and death made by oneself? Or by another? Or by both oneself and another? Or do they arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another?”

segs.p: “Na kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, sayaṅkataṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, na paraṅkataṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ, na sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca jarāmaraṇaṁ, nāpi asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ jarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: “No, Reverend Koṭṭhita, old age and death are not made by oneself, nor by another, nor by both oneself and another, nor do they arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
Rather, rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, sayaṅkatā jāti, paraṅkatā jāti, sayaṅkatā ca paraṅkatā ca jāti, udāhu asayaṅkārā aparaṅkārā adhiccasamuppannā jātī”ti?
segs.e: “Well, Reverend Sāriputta, is rebirth made by oneself? Or by another? Or by both oneself and another? Or does it arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another?”

segs.p: “Na kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, sayaṅkatā jāti, na paraṅkatā jāti, na sayaṅkatā ca paraṅkatā ca jāti, nāpi asayaṅkārā aparaṅkārā adhiccasamuppannā jāti.
segs.e: “No, Reverend Koṭṭhita, rebirth is not made by oneself, nor by another, nor by both oneself and another, nor does it arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
Rather, continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, sayaṅkato bhavo …pe…
segs.e: “Well, Reverend Sāriputta, is continued existence made by oneself? …” …
“Is grasping made by oneself? …” …
“Is craving made by oneself? …” …
“Is feeling made by oneself? …” …
“Is contact made by oneself? …” …
“Are the six sense fields made by oneself? …” …

segs.p: sayaṅkataṁ nāmarūpaṁ, paraṅkataṁ nāmarūpaṁ, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca nāmarūpaṁ, udāhu asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ nāmarūpan”ti?
segs.e: “Well, Reverend Sāriputta, are name and form made by oneself? Or by another? Or by both oneself and another? Or do they arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another?”

segs.p: “Na kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, sayaṅkataṁ nāmarūpaṁ, na paraṅkataṁ nāmarūpaṁ, na sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca nāmarūpaṁ, nāpi asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ, adhiccasamuppannaṁ nāmarūpaṁ.
segs.e: “No, Reverend Koṭṭhita, name and form are not made by oneself, nor by another, nor by both oneself and another, nor do they arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
Rather, consciousness is a requirement for name and form.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, sayaṅkataṁ viññāṇaṁ, paraṅkataṁ viññāṇaṁ, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca viññāṇaṁ, udāhu asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ viññāṇan”ti?
segs.e: “Well, Reverend Sāriputta, is consciousness made by oneself? Or by another? Or by both oneself and another? Or does it arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another?”

segs.p: “Na kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, sayaṅkataṁ viññāṇaṁ, na paraṅkataṁ viññāṇaṁ, na sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca viññāṇaṁ, nāpi asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ viññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: “No, Reverend Koṭṭhita, consciousness is not made by oneself, nor by another, nor by both oneself and another, nor does it arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
Rather, name and form are requirements for consciousness.”

segs.p: “Idāneva kho mayaṁ āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ evaṁ ājānāma:
segs.e: “Just now I understood you to say:

segs.p: ‘na khvāvuso koṭṭhika, sayaṅkataṁ nāmarūpaṁ, na paraṅkataṁ nāmarūpaṁ, na sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca nāmarūpaṁ, nāpi asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ nāmarūpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘No, Reverend Koṭṭhita, name and form are not made by oneself, nor by another, nor by both oneself and another, nor do they arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
Rather, consciousness is a requirement for name and form.’

segs.p: Idāneva ca pana mayaṁ āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ evaṁ ājānāma:
segs.e: But I also understood you to say:

segs.p: ‘na khvāvuso koṭṭhika, sayaṅkataṁ viññāṇaṁ, na paraṅkataṁ viññāṇaṁ, na sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca viññāṇaṁ, nāpi asayaṅkāraṁ aparaṅkāraṁ adhiccasamuppannaṁ viññāṇaṁ.
segs.e: ‘No, Reverend Koṭṭhita, consciousness is not made by oneself, nor by another, nor by both oneself and another, nor does it arise anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
Rather, name and form are requirements for consciousness.’

segs.p: Yathā kathaṁ panāvuso sāriputta, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
segs.e: How then should we see the meaning of this statement?”
“Well then, reverend, I shall give you a simile.

segs.p: Upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṁ jānanti.
segs.e: For by means of a simile some sensible people understand the meaning of what is said.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, dve naḷakalāpiyo aññamaññaṁ nissāya tiṭṭheyyuṁ.
segs.e: Suppose there were two sheaves of reeds leaning up against each other.
In the same way, name and form are requirements for consciousness.
Consciousness is a requirement for name and form.
Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields.
The six sense fields are requirements for contact. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

segs.p: Tāsañce, āvuso, naḷakalāpīnaṁ ekaṁ ākaḍḍheyya, ekā papateyya;
segs.e: If the first of those sheaves of reeds were to be pulled away, the other would collapse.
And if the other were to be pulled away, the first would collapse.
In the same way, when name and form cease, consciousness ceases.
When consciousness ceases, name and form cease.
When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease.
When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.”
“It’s incredible, Reverend Sāriputta, it’s amazing!
How well spoken this was by Venerable Sāriputta!

segs.p: Idañca pana mayaṁ āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ imehi chattiṁsāya vatthūhi anumodāma:
segs.e: And we can express our agreement with Venerable Sāriputta’s statement on these thirty-six grounds.

segs.p: ‘Jarāmaraṇassa ce, āvuso, bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, dhammakathiko bhikkhūti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding old age and death, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Jarāmaraṇassa ce, āvuso, bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhūti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding old age and death, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Jarāmaraṇassa ce, āvuso, bhikkhu nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti, diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhūti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they’re freed by not grasping by disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding old age and death, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who has attained extinguishment in this very life’.
If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment regarding rebirth …
continued existence …
grasping …
craving …
feeling …
contact …
the six sense fields …
name and form …
consciousness …
choices …

segs.p: avijjāya ce, āvuso, bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya dhammaṁ deseti, dhammakathiko bhikkhūti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If a mendicant teaches Dhamma for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding ignorance, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who speaks on Dhamma’.

segs.p: Avijjāya ce, āvuso, bhikkhu nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti, dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhūti alaṁvacanāya.
segs.e: If they practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding ignorance, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who practices in line with the teaching’.

segs.p: Avijjāya ce, āvuso, bhikkhu nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti, diṭṭhadhammanibbānappatto bhikkhūti alaṁvacanāyā’”ti.
segs.e: If they’re freed by not grasping by disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding ignorance, they’re qualified to be called ‘a mendicant who has attained extinguishment in this very life’.”
Linked Discourses 12.68
7. The Great Chapter
At Kosambī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca musilo āyasmā ca paviṭṭho āyasmā ca nārado āyasmā ca ānando kosambiyaṁ viharanti ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the venerables Musīla, Saviṭṭha, Nārada, and Ānanda were staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā paviṭṭho āyasmantaṁ musilaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Saviṭṭha said to Venerable Musīla:

segs.p: “aññatreva, āvuso musila, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato musilassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverend Musīla, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, do you personally know that
rebirth is a requirement for old age and death?”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, I know and see that
rebirth is a requirement for old age and death.”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso musila, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato musilassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverend Musīla, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberateation, do you personally know that
continued existence is a requirement for rebirth …
grasping is a requirement for continued existence …
craving is a requirement for grasping …
feeling is a requirement for craving …
contact is a requirement for feeling …
the six sense fields are requirements for contact …
name and form are requirements for the six sense fields …
consciousness is a requirement for name and form …
choices are a requirement for consciousness …
ignorance is a requirement for choices?”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, I know and see that
ignorance is a requirement for choices.”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso musila, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato musilassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverend Musīla, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, do you personally know that
when rebirth ceases, old age and death cease?”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, I know and see that
when rebirth ceases, old age and death cease.”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso musila, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato musilassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverend Musīla, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, do you personally know that
when continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases …
when grasping ceases, continued existence ceases …
when craving ceases, grasping ceases …
when feeling ceases, craving ceases …
when contact ceases, feeling ceases …
when the six sense fields cease, contact ceases …
when name and form cease, the six sense fields cease …
when consciousness ceases name and form cease …
when choices cease consciousness ceases …
when ignorance ceases, choices cease?”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, I know and see that
when ignorance ceases, choices cease.”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso musila, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato musilassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverend Musīla, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, do you personally know that
the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment?”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, I know and see that
the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment.”
“Then Venerable Musīla is a perfected one, with defilements ended.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā musilo tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: When he said this, Musīla kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā nārado āyasmantaṁ paviṭṭhaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Nārada said to Venerable Saviṭṭha,
“Reverend Saviṭṭha, please let me answer these questions.
Ask me
and I will answer them for you.”
“By all means, Venerable Nārada, try these questions.
I’ll ask you

segs.p: Byākarotu ca me āyasmā nārado etaṁ pañhaṁ.
segs.e: and you can answer them for me.”

segs.p: Aññatreva, āvuso nārada, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato nāradassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: (Saviṭṭha repeats exactly the same series of questions, and Nārada answers just as Musīla did.)

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
“Aññatreva, āvuso nārada, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato nāradassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ—
“Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
“Aññatreva, āvuso nārada, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato nāradassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
“Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
“Aññatreva, āvuso nārada, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato nāradassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
“Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
“Aññatreva, āvuso nārada, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā atthāyasmato nāradassa paccattameva ñāṇaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverend Nārada, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, do you personally know that
the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment?”

segs.p: “Aññatreva, āvuso paviṭṭha, saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā ahametaṁ jānāmi ahametaṁ passāmi:
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, apart from faith, endorsement, oral transmission, reasoned train of thought, or acceptance of a view after deliberation, I know and see that
the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment.”
“Then Venerable Nārada is a perfected one, with defilements ended.”

segs.p: “‘Bhavanirodho nibbānan’ti kho me, āvuso, yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ, na camhi arahaṁ khīṇāsavo.
segs.e: “I have truly seen clearly with right wisdom that the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment. Yet I am not a perfected one.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, kantāramagge udapāno, tatra nevassa rajju na udakavārako.
segs.e: Suppose there was a well on a desert road that had neither rope nor bucket.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito, so taṁ udapānaṁ olokeyya.
segs.e: Then along comes a person struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.

segs.p: Tassa ‘udakan’ti hi kho ñāṇaṁ assa, na ca kāyena phusitvā vihareyya.
segs.e: They’d know that there was water, but they couldn’t physically touch it.

segs.p: Evameva kho, āvuso, ‘bhavanirodho nibbānan’ti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṁ, na camhi arahaṁ khīṇāsavo”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, I have truly seen clearly with right wisdom that the cessation of continued existence is extinguishment. Yet I am not a perfected one.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ paviṭṭhaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to Venerable Saviṭṭha,

segs.p: “evaṁvādī tvaṁ, āvuso paviṭṭha, āyasmantaṁ nāradaṁ kiṁ vadesī”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, what do you have to say to Venerable Nārada when he speaks like this?”

segs.p: “Evaṁvādāhaṁ, āvuso ānanda, āyasmantaṁ nāradaṁ na kiñci vadāmi aññatra kalyāṇā aññatra kusalā”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, I have nothing to say to Venerable Nārada when he speaks like this, except what is good and wholesome.”
Linked Discourses 12.69
7. The Great Chapter
Surge
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: “mahāsamuddo, bhikkhave, upayanto mahānadiyo upayāpeti, mahānadiyo upayantiyo kunnadiyo upayāpenti, kunnadiyo upayantiyo mahāsobbhe upayāpenti, mahāsobbhā upayantā kusobbhe upayāpenti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when the ocean surges it makes the rivers surge. When the rivers surge they make the streams surge. When the streams surge they make the lakes surge. When the lakes surge they make the ponds surge.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, avijjā upayantī saṅkhāre upayāpeti, saṅkhārā upayantā viññāṇaṁ upayāpenti, viññāṇaṁ upayantaṁ nāmarūpaṁ upayāpeti, nāmarūpaṁ upayantaṁ saḷāyatanaṁ upayāpeti, saḷāyatanaṁ upayantaṁ phassaṁ upayāpeti, phasso upayanto vedanaṁ upayāpeti, vedanā upayantī taṇhaṁ upayāpeti, taṇhā upayantī upādānaṁ upayāpeti, upādānaṁ upayantaṁ bhavaṁ upayāpeti, bhavo upayanto jātiṁ upayāpeti, jāti upayantī jarāmaraṇaṁ upayāpeti.
segs.e: In the same way, when ignorance surges it makes choices surge. When choices surge they make consciousness surge. When consciousness surges it makes name and form surge. When name and form surge they make the six sense fields surge. When the six sense fields surge they make contact surge. When contact surges it makes feeling surge. When feeling surges it makes craving surge. When craving surges it makes grasping surge. When grasping surges it makes continued existence surge. When continued existence surges it makes rebirth surge. When rebirth surges it makes old age and death surge.

segs.p: Mahāsamuddo, bhikkhave, apayanto mahānadiyo apayāpeti, mahānadiyo apayantiyo kunnadiyo apayāpenti, kunnadiyo apayantiyo mahāsobbhe apayāpenti, mahāsobbhā apayantā kusobbhe apayāpenti.
segs.e: When the ocean recedes it makes the rivers recede. When the rivers recede they make the streams recede. When the streams recede they make the lakes recede. When the lakes recede they make the ponds recede.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, avijjā apayantī saṅkhāre apayāpeti, saṅkhārā apayantā viññāṇaṁ apayāpenti, viññāṇaṁ apayantaṁ nāmarūpaṁ apayāpeti, nāmarūpaṁ apayantaṁ saḷāyatanaṁ apayāpeti, saḷāyatanaṁ apayantaṁ phassaṁ apayāpeti, phasso apayanto vedanaṁ apayāpeti, vedanā apayantī taṇhaṁ apayāpeti, taṇhā apayantī upādānaṁ apayāpeti, upādānaṁ apayantaṁ bhavaṁ apayāpeti, bhavo apayanto jātiṁ apayāpeti, jāti apayantī jarāmaraṇaṁ apayāpetī”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, when ignorance recedes it makes choices recede. When choices recede they make consciousness recede. When consciousness recedes it makes name and form recede. When name and form recede they make the six sense fields recede. When the six sense fields recede they make contact recede. When contact recedes it makes feeling recede. When feeling recedes it makes craving recede. When craving recedes it makes grasping recede. When grasping recedes it makes continued existence recede. When continued existence recedes it makes rebirth recede. When rebirth recedes it makes old age and death recede.”
Linked Discourses 12.70
7. The Great Chapter
The Wanderer Susīma
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And he received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Bhikkhusaṅghopi sakkato hoti garukato mānito pūjito apacito lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: And the mendicant Saṅgha was also honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Aññatitthiyā pana paribbājakā asakkatā honti agarukatā amānitā apūjitā anapacitā, na lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
segs.e: But the wanderers who followed other religions were not honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And they didn’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena susimo paribbājako rājagahe paṭivasati mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time the wanderer Susīma was residing at Rājagaha together with a large community of wanderers.

segs.p: Atha kho susimassa paribbājakassa parisā susimaṁ paribbājakaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then his community said to Susīma,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, āvuso susima, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṁ cara.
segs.e: “Reverend Susīma, please lead the spiritual life with the ascetic Gotama.
Memorize that teaching and have us recite it with you.

segs.p: Taṁ mayaṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā gihīnaṁ bhāsissāma.
segs.e: When we’ve memorized it we’ll recite it to the laity.

segs.p: Evaṁ mayampi sakkatā bhavissāma garukatā mānitā pūjitā apacitā lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānan”ti.
segs.e: In this way we too will be honored, respected, revered, venerated, and esteemed. And we’ll receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho susimo paribbājako sakāya parisāya paṭissuṇitvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverends,” replied Susīma to his own assembly. Then he went to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho susimo paribbājako āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Ānanda,

segs.p: “icchāmahaṁ, āvuso ānanda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye brahmacariyaṁ caritun”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, I wish to lead the spiritual life in this teaching and training.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando susimaṁ paribbājakaṁ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ānanda took Susīma to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, this wanderer Susīma says that

segs.p: ‘icchāmahaṁ, āvuso ānanda, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye brahmacariyaṁ caritun’”ti.
segs.e: he wishes to lead the spiritual life in this teaching and training.”
“Well then, Ānanda, give Susīma the going forth.”

segs.p: Alattha kho susimo paribbājako bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And the wanderer Susīma received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulehi bhikkhūhi bhagavato santike aññā byākatā hoti:
segs.e: Now at that time several mendicants had declared their enlightenment in the Buddha’s presence:

segs.p: “khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāmā”ti.
segs.e: “We understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”
Venerable Susīma heard about this.

segs.p: “sambahulehi kira bhikkhūhi bhagavato santike aññā byākatā:
‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā”ti.
Atha kho āyasmā susimo yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: He went up to those mendicants, and exchanged greetings with them.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā susimo te bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to those mendicants,
“Is it really true that the venerables have declared enlightenment in the Buddha’s presence?”

segs.p: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā”ti?

segs.e: “Yes, reverend.”

segs.p: “Api pana tumhe āyasmanto evaṁ jānantā evaṁ passantā anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhotha—ekopi hutvā bahudhā hotha, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hotha; āvibhāvaṁ, tirobhāvaṁ, tirokuṭṭaṁ tiropākāraṁ tiropabbataṁ asajjamānā gacchatha, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karotha, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchatha, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamatha, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasatha parimajjatha, yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vattethā”ti?
segs.e: “But knowing and seeing thus, do you wield the many kinds of psychic power? That is, multiplying yourselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. Do you control the body as far as the realm of divinity?”
“No, reverend.”

segs.p: “Api pana tumhe āyasmanto evaṁ jānantā evaṁ passantā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇātha dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike cā”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus do you, with clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far?”
“No, reverend.”

segs.p: “Api pana tumhe āyasmanto evaṁ jānantā evaṁ passantā parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānātha—
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with your mind?

segs.p: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand mind with greed as ‘mind with greed’,

segs.p: vītarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ vītarāgaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and mind without greed as ‘mind without greed’?

segs.p: sadosaṁ vā cittaṁ sadosaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand mind with hate as ‘mind with hate’,

segs.p: vītadosaṁ vā cittaṁ vītadosaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and mind without hate as ‘mind without hate’?

segs.p: samohaṁ vā cittaṁ samohaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand mind with delusion as ‘mind with delusion’,

segs.p: vītamohaṁ vā cittaṁ vītamohaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and mind without delusion as ‘mind without delusion’?

segs.p: saṅkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ saṅkhittaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand constricted mind as ‘constricted mind’,

segs.p: vikkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ vikkhittaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and scattered mind as ‘scattered mind’?

segs.p: mahaggataṁ vā cittaṁ mahaggataṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand expansive mind as ‘expansive mind’,

segs.p: amahaggataṁ vā cittaṁ amahaggataṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and unexpansive mind as ‘unexpansive mind’?

segs.p: sauttaraṁ vā cittaṁ sauttaraṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand mind that is not supreme as ‘mind that is not supreme’,

segs.p: anuttaraṁ vā cittaṁ anuttaraṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and mind that is supreme as ‘mind that is supreme’?

segs.p: samāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ samāhitaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand mind immersed in samādhi as ‘mind immersed in samādhi’,

segs.p: asamāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ asamāhitaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: and mind not immersed in samādhi as ‘mind not immersed in samādhi’?

segs.p: vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ cittanti pajānātha;
segs.e: Do you understand freed mind as ‘freed mind’,

segs.p: avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāthā”ti?
segs.e: and unfreed mind as ‘unfreed mind’?”
“No, reverend.”

segs.p: “Api pana tumhe āyasmanto evaṁ jānantā evaṁ passantā anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussaratha, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṁsampi jātiyo cattārīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi, anekepi saṁvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṁvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe: ‘amutrāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhapaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṁ; tatrāpāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhapaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarathā”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you recollect many kinds of past lives? That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding? Do you remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ Do you recollect your many kinds of past lives, with features and details?”
“No, reverend.”

segs.p: “Api pana tumhe āyasmanto evaṁ jānantā evaṁ passantā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passatha cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānātha: ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā, ariyānaṁ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā, ariyānaṁ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā’ti, iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passatha cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāthā”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place—and understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds? ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, do you see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. And do you understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds?”
“No, reverend.”

segs.p: “Api pana tumhe āyasmanto evaṁ jānantā evaṁ passantā ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā, te kāyena phusitvā viharathā”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form?”
“No, reverend.”

segs.p: “Ettha dāni āyasmanto idañca veyyākaraṇaṁ imesañca dhammānaṁ asamāpatti; idaṁ no, āvuso, kathan”ti?
segs.e: “Well now, venerables, how could there be such a declaration when these things are not attained?”
“Reverend Susīma, we are freed by wisdom.”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ imassa āyasmantānaṁ saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: “I don’t understand the detailed meaning of what you have said in brief.

segs.p: Sādhu me āyasmanto tathā bhāsantu yathāhaṁ imassa āyasmantānaṁ saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājāneyyan”ti.
segs.e: Please teach me this matter so I can understand the detailed meaning.”

segs.p: “Ājāneyyāsi vā tvaṁ, āvuso susima, na vā tvaṁ ājāneyyāsi atha kho paññāvimuttā mayan”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Susīma, whether you understand or not, we are freed by wisdom.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā susimo uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Susīma went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā susimo yāvatako tehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ ahosi kathāsallāpo taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesi.
segs.e: and informed the Buddha of all he had discussed with those mendicants.

segs.p: “Pubbe kho, susima, dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṁ, pacchā nibbāne ñāṇan”ti.
segs.e: “Susīma, first comes knowledge of the stability of natural principles. Afterwards there is knowledge of extinguishment.”

segs.p: “Na khvāhaṁ, bhante, imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
segs.e: “Sir, I don’t understand the detailed meaning of what you have said in brief.

segs.p: Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā bhāsatu yathāhaṁ imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājāneyyan”ti.
segs.e: Please teach me this matter so I can understand the detailed meaning.”

segs.p: “Ājāneyyāsi vā tvaṁ, susima, na vā tvaṁ ājāneyyāsi, atha kho dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṁ pubbe, pacchā nibbāne ñāṇaṁ.
segs.e: “Susīma, whether you understand or not, first comes knowledge of the stability of natural principles. Afterwards there is knowledge of extinguishment.
What do you think, Susīma?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is feeling permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is perception permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …
“Are choices permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if they’re impermanent, are they suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if they’re impermanent, suffering, and perishable, are they fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
segs.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Tasmātiha, susima, yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ netaṁ mama nesohamasmi na meso attāti; evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: “So, Susīma, you should truly see any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, sabbā vedanā netaṁ mama nesohamasmi na meso attāti; evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should truly see any kind of feeling at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all feeling—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

You should truly see any kind of perception at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all perception—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā ye dūre santike vā, sabbe saṅkhārā netaṁ mama nesohamasmi na meso attāti; evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should truly see any kind of choices at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all choices—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ netaṁ mama nesohamasmi na meso attāti; evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should truly see any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ passaṁ, susima, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
segs.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

segs.p: Nibbindaṁ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati, vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’
Susīma, do you see that rebirth is a requirement for old age and death?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that continued existence is a requirement for rebirth?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that grasping is a requirement for continued existence?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that craving is a requirement for grasping?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that feeling is a requirement for craving …
contact is a requirement for feeling …
the six sense fields are requirements for contact …
name and form are requirements for the six sense fields …
consciousness is a requirement for name and form …
choices are a requirement for consciousness …
ignorance is a requirement for choices?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that when rebirth ceases old age and death cease?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that when continued existence ceases rebirth ceases?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Do you see that when grasping ceases continued existence ceases …
when craving ceases, grasping ceases …
when feeling ceases, craving ceases …
when contact ceases, feeling ceases …
when the six sense fields cease, contact ceases …
when name and form cease, the six sense fields cease …
when consciousness ceases name and form cease …
when choices cease consciousness ceases …
when ignorance ceases choices cease?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Api pana tvaṁ, susima, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhosi—ekopi hutvā bahudhā hosi, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hosi; āvibhāvaṁ, tirobhāvaṁ, tirokuṭṭaṁ tiropākāraṁ tiropabbataṁ asajjamāno gacchasi, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karosi, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāno gacchasi, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamasi, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasasi parimajjasi, yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vattesī”ti?
segs.e: “But knowing and seeing thus, do you wield the many kinds of psychic power? …”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Api pana tvaṁ, susima, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇasi dibbe ca mānuse ca ye dūre santike cā”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus do you, with clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Api pana tvaṁ, susima, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāsi—
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with your mind? …”

segs.p: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāsi …pe…
vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāsī”ti?

segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Api pana tvaṁ, susima, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarasi, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarasī”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Api pana tvaṁ, susima, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passasi cavamāne …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāsī”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, see sentient beings passing away and being reborn … according to their deeds?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Api pana tvaṁ, susima, evaṁ jānanto evaṁ passanto ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā, te kāyena phusitvā viharasī”ti?
segs.e: “Well, knowing and seeing thus, do you have direct meditative experience of the peaceful liberations that are formless, transcending form?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ettha dāni, susima, idañca veyyākaraṇaṁ imesañca dhammānaṁ asamāpatti, idaṁ no, susima, kathan”ti?
segs.e: “Well now, Susīma, how could there be such a declaration when these things are not attained?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā susimo bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Susīma bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet and said,

segs.p: “accayo maṁ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yvāhaṁ evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye dhammatthenako pabbajito.
segs.e: “I made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of me to go forth as a thief in such a well-explained teaching and training.

segs.p: Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṁ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṁ saṁvarāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please, sir, accept my mistake for what it is, so I will restrain myself in future.”

segs.p: “Taggha tvaṁ, susima, accayo accagamā yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yo tvaṁ evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye dhammatthenako pabbajito.
segs.e: “Indeed, Susīma, you made a mistake. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to go forth as a thief of the teachings in such a well-explained teaching and training.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, susima, coraṁ āgucāriṁ gahetvā rañño dasseyyuṁ:
segs.e: Suppose they were to arrest a bandit, a criminal and present him to the king, saying:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ te, deva, coro āgucārī, imassa yaṁ icchasi taṁ daṇḍaṁ paṇehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Your Majesty, this is a bandit, a criminal. Punish him as you will.’
The king would say:

segs.p: ‘gacchatha, bho, imaṁ purisaṁ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṁ gāḷhabandhanaṁ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṁ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathiyāya rathiyaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sīsaṁ chindathā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Go, my men, and tie this man’s arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope. Shave his head and march him from street to street and from square to square to the beating of a harsh drum. Then take him out the south gate and there, to the south of the city, chop off his head.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rañño purisā daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṁ gāḷhabandhanaṁ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṁ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathiyāya rathiyaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sīsaṁ chindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: The king’s men would do as they were told.
What do you think, Susīma?

segs.p: api nu so puriso tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvediyethā”ti?
segs.e: Wouldn’t that man experience pain and distress because of that?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho so, susima, puriso tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvediyetha.
segs.e: “Although that man would experience pain and distress because of that,
